sentences.zh: 楊玄感楊玄感，司徒素之子也。

translations.literal: Yang Xuangan was the son of Yang Su, Duke of Situ.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan was the son of Yang Su, who had held the post of Minister of Works and the title Duke of Situ.

sentences.zh: 體貌雄偉，美鬚髯。

translations.literal: His physique was imposing and majestic, and he had a fine beard and whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: He was powerfully built and striking in appearance, with a splendid beard.

sentences.zh: 少時晚成，人多謂之癡，其父每謂所親曰：「此兒不癡也。」

translations.literal: In youth he matured late, and many called him dull; his father would often say to those close to him, "This boy is not dull.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was slow to show his abilities, and many took him for a simpleton; his father would often tell intimates, "This son of mine is no fool.

sentences.zh: 及長，好讀書，便騎射。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he loved reading and was skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he took to study and proved adept at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 以父軍功，位至柱國，與其父俱為第二品，朝會則齊列。

translations.literal: By his father's military merit he rose to the rank of Pillar of State; he and his father were both of the second grade, and at court assemblies they stood in the same row.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his father's battlefield honors he attained the rank of Pillar of State; father and son alike held second-grade emoluments and took their places side by side at court.

sentences.zh: 其後高祖命玄感降一等，玄感拜謝曰：「不意陛下寵臣之甚，許以公廷獲展私敬。」

translations.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu ordered Xuangan reduced one grade; Xuangan bowed in thanks and said, "I did not expect Your Majesty to favor your servant so greatly as to allow display of private respect in the public court.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gaozu had Xuangan lowered one rank in precedence. Xuangan bowed his thanks and said, "I never imagined Your Majesty would honor me so far as to let me show filial regard even in the formal court.

sentences.zh: 初拜郢州刺史，到官，潛布耳目，察長吏能不。

translations.literal: When first appointed regional inspector of Yingzhou, upon taking office he secretly set up informants to observe the ability and incapacity of senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: On his first appointment as inspector of Yingzhou he quietly placed observers to test whether local administrators were competent or corrupt.

sentences.zh: 其有善政及贓污者，纖介必知之，往往發其事，莫敢欺隱。

translations.literal: Whether they had good administration or embezzlement, he would know the minutest detail and often expose the matter; none dared conceal anything.
translations.idiomatic: Good governance and graft alike he came to know down to the smallest particular, and he was apt to bring abuses to light so that none could hide them.

sentences.zh: 吏民敬服，皆稱其能。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners revered and obeyed him, all calling him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people alike stood in awe of him and acclaimed his ability.

sentences.zh: 後轉宋州刺史，父憂去職。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to regional inspector of Songzhou and left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was later moved to Songzhou as inspector, then resigned to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起拜鴻臚卿，襲爵楚國公，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled and appointed Chamberlain for Dependencies, inherited the title Duke of Chu, and was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was recalled as Chamberlain for Dependencies, succeeded to the dukedom of Chu, and was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 性雖驕倨，而愛重文學，四海知名之士多趨其門。

translations.literal: Though by nature arrogant, he prized and honored letters; celebrated scholars from the four seas many flocked to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: For all his pride he cultivated learning, and men of renown from across the realm thronged his house.

sentences.zh: 自以累世尊顯，有盛名於天下，在朝文武多是父之將吏，復見朝綱漸紊，帝又猜忌日甚，內不自安，遂與諸弟潛謀廢帝，立秦王浩。

translations.literal: Considering himself of many generations' eminent display, with great fame under heaven, and that most civil and military officials at court had been his father's generals and officers, and seeing court discipline gradually disordered and the emperor's suspicion daily increasing, inwardly ill at ease, he therefore with his brothers secretly plotted to depose the emperor and enthrone Prince Qin Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Conscious of his family's generations of glory and his own fame throughout the realm, and that many at court had once served under his father, he watched the court slip into disorder and the emperor grow ever more suspicious. Uneasy at heart, he and his brothers secretly planned to remove the emperor and install Prince Qin Hao.

sentences.zh: 及從征吐谷渾，還至大斗拔谷，時從官狼狽，玄感欲襲擊行宮。

translations.literal: When following the campaign against Tuyuhun and returning to Dabopeng Valley, at that time the attendant officials were in distress; Xuangan wished to strike the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tuyuhun campaign, marching back through Dabopeng Valley when the court was in disarray, he contemplated a surprise attack on the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 其叔慎謂玄感曰：「士心尚一，國未有釁，不可圖也。」

translations.literal: His uncle Shen said to Xuangan, "The hearts of the officers are still united, and the state has no breach—this cannot be plotted.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yang Shen told him, "The army is still of one mind and the realm shows no crack in its order—you must not attempt this.

sentences.zh: 玄感乃止。

translations.literal: Xuangan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 時帝好征伐，玄感欲立威名，陰求將領。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor loved campaigns; Xuangan wished to establish a martial reputation and secretly sought a command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was bent on military campaigns, and Xuangan, eager to win a name in arms, quietly sought a field command.

sentences.zh: 謂兵部尚書段文振曰：「玄感世荷國恩，寵踰涯分，自非立效邊裔，何以塞責！

translations.literal: He said to Minister of War Duan Wenzhen, "Xuangan has for generations received the state's grace, and favor has exceeded the bounds of my station; unless I establish merit on the frontier, how can I discharge my obligation!
translations.idiomatic: He told Minister of War Duan Wenzhen, "My family has long enjoyed the state's favor, and I have been honored beyond my deserts. Unless I win distinction on the frontier, how can I answer for myself!

sentences.zh: 若方隅有風塵之警，庶得執鞭行陣，少展絲髮之功。

translations.literal: If the border regions should have alarms of war, I might hope to hold the whip in the ranks and show a hair's breadth of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Should trouble flare on the marches, I might at least serve in the ranks and offer whatever small service I can.

sentences.zh: 明公兵革是司，敢布心腹。」

translations.literal: Your Excellency is in charge of arms; I venture to lay bare my inmost thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: As you oversee military affairs, I take the liberty of speaking to you frankly.

sentences.zh: 文振因言於帝，帝嘉之，顧謂羣臣曰：「將門必有將，相門必有相，故不虛也。」

translations.literal: Wenzhen thereupon spoke to the emperor, and the emperor commended him; turning to the assembled ministers he said, "A general's house must produce a general, a minister's house a minister—the saying is not empty."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen relayed this to the emperor, who was pleased and told the court, "A general's house breeds generals, a minister's house breeds ministers—the proverb is true."

sentences.zh: 於是賚物千段，禮遇益隆，頗預朝政。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was bestowed a thousand lengths of goods, his ceremonial treatment grew ever more lofty, and he took considerable part in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with a thousand lengths of silk, his honors increased, and he came to take a considerable hand in court affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝征遼東，命玄感於黎陽督運。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned against Liaodong and ordered Xuangan to supervise transport at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched against Liaodong, he put Xuangan in charge of supply transport at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 于時百姓苦役，天下思亂，玄感遂與武賁郎將王仲伯、汲郡贊治趙懷義等謀議，欲令帝所軍眾飢餒，每為逗遛，不時進發。

translations.literal: At that time the common people suffered under corvée, and the realm yearned for disorder; Xuangan then with Majordomo Wang Zhongbo, Jijun Administrator Zhao Huaiyi, and others plotted, wishing to make the emperor's armies hungry and starved, always delaying and not dispatching supplies on time.
translations.idiomatic: The people were ground down by forced labor and rebellion was in the air. Xuangan conspired with Majordomo Wang Zhongbo, Jijun Administrator Zhao Huaiyi, and others to starve the armies in the field by holding back shipments and never sending supplies on schedule.

sentences.zh: 帝遲之，遣使者逼促，玄感揚言曰：「水路多盜賊，不可前後而發。」

translations.literal: The emperor grew impatient and sent envoys to press him; Xuangan proclaimed publicly, "The waterways have many bandits—it is not possible to dispatch convoys in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew impatient and sent envoys to hurry him, Xuangan announced publicly, "Pirates infest the waterways—we cannot risk sending convoys one after another.

sentences.zh: 其弟武賁郎將玄縱、鷹揚郎將萬碩並從幸遼東，玄感潛遣人召之。

translations.literal: His brothers Majordomo Xu Zong and General Wan Shuo were both accompanying the emperor in Liaodong; Xuangan secretly sent men to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Xu Zong, a majordomo, and Wan Shuo, a general, were both with the emperor in Liaodong, and Xuangan secretly summoned them.

sentences.zh: 時將軍來護兒以舟師自東萊將入海，趣平壤城，軍未發。

translations.literal: At that time General Lai Huer with a fleet from Donglai was about to put to sea and hasten to Pyongyang; the army had not yet set out.
translations.idiomatic: General Lai Huer was about to sail from Donglai with a fleet toward Pyongyang, but his force had not yet embarked.

sentences.zh: 玄感無以動眾，乃遣家奴偽為使者，從東方來，謬稱護兒失軍期而反。

translations.literal: Xuangan had no means to stir the masses, so he sent a household slave disguised as an envoy from the east, falsely announcing that Huer had missed his campaign deadline and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to rally the people on his own authority, he sent a household slave posing as a courier from the east with a false report that Lai Huer had missed his deadline and turned rebel.

sentences.zh: 玄感遂入黎陽縣，閉城大索男夫。

translations.literal: Xuangan then entered Liyang county, closed the city, and conducted a great search for able-bodied men.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan then seized Liyang county, shut the gates, and pressed every able-bodied man into service.

sentences.zh: 於是取帆布為牟甲，署官屬，皆準開皇之舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon they took sailcloth for armor, appointed officials, all according to the Kaihuang precedents.
translations.idiomatic: They fashioned armor from sailcloth, appointed officials, and organized their regime on the model of the Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 移書傍郡，以討護兒為名，各令發兵，會於倉所。

translations.literal: He sent letters to neighboring commanderies, in the name of punishing Huer ordering each to raise troops and assemble at the granary.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to neighboring prefectures, calling on them to raise troops to punish Lai Huer and muster at the granary depot.

sentences.zh: 以東光縣尉元務本為黎州刺史，趙懷義為衞州刺史，河內郡主簿唐禕為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: He made Dongguang county magistrate Yuan Wuben regional inspector of Liyang, Zhao Huaiyi regional inspector of Weizhou, and Henei chief clerk Tang Yi regional inspector of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yuan Wuben, magistrate of Dongguang, inspector of Liyang; Zhao Huaiyi, inspector of Weizhou; and Tang Yi, chief clerk of Henei, inspector of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 有眾且一萬，將襲洛陽。

translations.literal: He had a force of nearly ten thousand and was about to strike Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: With nearly ten thousand men he prepared to march on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 唐禕至河內，馳往東都告之。

translations.literal: Tang Yi reached Henei and galloped to the Eastern Capital to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yi reached Henei and rode at full speed to the Eastern Capital to raise the alarm.

sentences.zh: 越王侗、民部尚書樊子蓋等大懼，勒兵備禦。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Yang Tong, Minister of Population Fan Zigai, and others were greatly afraid and mustered troops to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Yang Tong, Minister of Population Fan Zigai, and the court were thrown into panic and hurried to mobilize for defense.

sentences.zh: 修武縣民相率守臨清關，玄感不得濟，遂於汲郡南渡河，從亂者如市。

translations.literal: The people of Xiuwu county together guarded Linqing Pass; Xuangan could not cross, so south of Jijun he crossed the river, and those who followed the rebellion were like a market crowd.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xiuwu barred Linqing Pass, blocking his crossing; he forded the river south of Jijun, and rebels flocked to him in throngs.

sentences.zh: 數日，屯兵上春門，眾至十餘萬。

translations.literal: Within days he encamped at Shangchun Gate, and his forces reached more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he had encamped at Shangchun Gate with a host of more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 子蓋令河南贊治裴弘策拒之，弘策戰敗。

translations.literal: Zigai ordered Henan Administrator Pei Hongce to resist him; Hongce was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai sent Henan Administrator Pei Hongce to oppose him, but Hongce was routed.

sentences.zh: 瀍、洛父老競致牛酒。

translations.literal: The elders of the Chan and Luo districts vied to present oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Elders along the Chan and Luo rivers competed to bring cattle and wine in welcome.

sentences.zh: 玄感屯兵尚書省，每誓眾曰：「我身為上柱國，家累鉅萬金，至於富貴，無所求也。

translations.literal: Xuangan encamped his troops at the Ministry of State Affairs; each time he addressed the masses he said, "I personally am a Pillar of State, and my household accumulates tens of thousands in gold—as to wealth and honor, I seek nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan quartered his army in the Ministry of State Affairs compound and told his followers at each rally, "I am already a Pillar of State, and my house holds wealth beyond counting—in rank and riches I want for nothing.

sentences.zh: 今者不顧破家滅族者，但為天下解倒懸之急，救黎元之命耳。」

translations.literal: Now I disregard the destruction of house and clan only to relieve the realm's peril of hanging upside down and save the black-haired people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: I risk ruin for my house and clan only to lift the empire from its desperate plight and save the lives of the common people.

sentences.zh: 眾皆悅，詣轅門請自效者，日有數千。

translations.literal: The masses were all pleased, and those who came to the camp gate daily to offer their service numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd cheered him, and thousands each day presented themselves at his gate to enlist.

sentences.zh: 與樊子蓋書曰：

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Fan Zigai, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Fan Zigai:

sentences.zh: :夫建忠立義，事有多途，見機而作，蓋非一揆。

translations.literal: To establish loyalty and righteousness has many paths; to act when one sees the opportunity is surely not of one measure alone.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and righteous action may take many forms, and seizing the moment admits more than one right course.

sentences.zh: 昔伊尹放太甲於桐宮，霍光廢劉賀於昌邑，此並公度內，不能一二披陳。

translations.literal: Formerly Yi Yin placed Tai Jia in the Tong Palace, and Huo Guang deposed Liu He at Changyi—these were all within public propriety; I cannot set forth each in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin once confined Tai Jia in the Tong Palace; Huo Guang deposed Liu He at Changyi—both acted within the bounds of public duty. I cannot rehearse every precedent here.

sentences.zh: :高祖文皇帝誕膺天命，造茲區宇，在琁璣以齊七政，握金鏡以馭六龍，無為而至化流，垂拱而天下治。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Gaozu received Heaven's mandate and created this realm; stationed at the Celestial Pivot he aligned the seven regulators, grasped the golden mirror to drive the six dragons; through non-action transformation flowed, and with folded arms the realm was governed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen received the Mandate, founded this realm, aligned the heavens from his throne, and ruled as if holding a golden mirror to the age—through effortless governance the empire was transformed, and with hands at rest he brought order under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今上纂承寶曆，宜固洪基，乃自絕於天，殄民敗德。

translations.literal: The present sovereign inherited the precious succession and ought to consolidate the great foundation, yet he has cut himself off from Heaven, destroyed the people, and ruined virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor should have secured the throne his forebear left him, but he has turned his back on Heaven, ruining his people and his own virtue.

sentences.zh: 頻年肆眚，盜賊於是滋多，所在修治，民力為之凋盡。

translations.literal: Year after year he indulged in amnesties, and bandits thereby multiplied; everywhere construction and repair were carried out, and the people's strength was exhausted for it.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated amnesties have only bred more outlaws, and endless public works have drained the people to the bone.

sentences.zh: 荒淫酒色，子女必被其侵，躭玩鷹犬，禽獸皆離其毒。

translations.literal: Dissolute in wine and women, sons and daughters must suffer his encroachments; addicted to hawks and hounds, birds and beasts all flee his cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: He debauches himself with wine and women, preying on the young; he dotes on hawks and hounds, and even beasts flee his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 朋黨相扇，貨賄公行，納邪佞之言，杜正直之口。

translations.literal: Factions fanned one another, bribes walked openly in public, wicked and fawning words were admitted, and upright mouths were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Factions egg one another on, bribery is open in the streets, flatterers are heard and honest men silenced.

sentences.zh: 加以轉輸不息，徭役無期，士卒填溝壑，骸骨蔽原野。

translations.literal: Added to this, transport never ceased and corvée had no end; soldiers filled the ditches and gullies, and bones covered the open fields.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this, supply convoys never stop and corvée knows no end—soldiers fill the ditches and bones litter the fields.

sentences.zh: 黃河之北，則千里無煙，江淮之間，則鞠為茂草。

translations.literal: North of the Yellow River, for a thousand li there was no smoke; between the Jiang and Huai, all was rank with tall grass.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yellow River the land lies smokeless for a thousand li; between the Yangzi and Huai, fields have gone to wilderness.

sentences.zh: :玄感世荷國恩，位居上將，先公奉遺詔曰：「好子孫為我輔弼之，惡子孫為我屏黜之。」

translations.literal: Xuangan has for generations received the state's grace and stands in the rank of chief general; my late father received the testamentary edict saying, "Let good descendants assist me, and let wicked descendants be removed and cast out for me.
translations.idiomatic: My family has long enjoyed the state's favor, and I hold the rank of chief general. My late father was charged by the late emperor's testament: "Let worthy descendants support the throne; let unworthy ones be cast out.

sentences.zh: 所以上禀先旨，下順民心，廢此淫昏，更立明哲。

translations.literal: Therefore above I carry out my forebear's intent, below I accord with the people's hearts, deposing this dissolute dullard and installing a wise and enlightened ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore obey my father's charge and the people's will, removing this dissolute ruler and setting a wise man in his place.

sentences.zh: 四海同心，九州響應，士卒用命，如赴私讎，民庶相趨，義形公道。

translations.literal: The four seas are of one heart, the nine provinces echo in response; soldiers employ their lives as if rushing to a private feud, and the people hasten together, righteousness taking form in public justice.
translations.idiomatic: All within the seas are united, the provinces answer as one; soldiers fight as if settling a private score, and the people flock to the cause in the name of justice.

sentences.zh: 天意人事，較然可知。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent and human affairs are clearly comparable and knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's will and the people's mind are plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 公獨守孤城，勢何支久！

translations.literal: Your Excellency alone holds an isolated city—how long can such a position endure!
translations.idiomatic: You alone hold a doomed city—how long can you last?!

sentences.zh: 願以黔黎在念，社稷為心，勿拘小禮，自貽伊戚。

translations.literal: I wish you would keep the black-haired people in mind and take the altars of soil and grain to heart; do not be bound by petty ritual and bring calamity upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Think of the people and the realm; do not cling to petty loyalty and bring ruin on yourself.

sentences.zh: 誰謂國家一旦至此，執筆潸泫，言無所具。

translations.literal: Who would have said the state could come to this in a single day—I take up the brush with tears streaming, and words fail to set it forth.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have imagined the realm brought so low? My pen trembles with tears, and words are not enough.

sentences.zh: 遂進逼都城。

translations.literal: He then advanced and pressed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed the attack on the capital.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書衞玄，率眾數萬，自關中來援東都。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Wei Xuan led several tens of thousands from Guanzhong to relieve the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Wei Xuan marched from Guanzhong with tens of thousands to relieve the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 以步騎二萬渡瀍、澗挑戰，玄感偽北。

translations.literal: With twenty thousand infantry and cavalry he crossed the Chan and Jian rivers to offer battle; Xuangan feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Chan and Jian with twenty thousand foot and horse to give battle; Xuangan feigned a retreat.

sentences.zh: 玄逐之，伏兵發，前軍盡沒。

translations.literal: Xuan pursued him; ambush troops sprang up, and the vanguard was entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei pursued, ambush troops rose, and the vanguard was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 後數日，玄復與玄感戰，兵始合，玄感詐令人大呼曰：「官軍已得玄感矣。」

translations.literal: Several days later Xuan again fought Xuangan; as the armies had just joined battle, Xuangan had men falsely shout, "The government army has captured Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Wei engaged him again. As the lines met, Xuangan had men shout falsely, "The imperial army has taken Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 玄軍稍怠。

translations.literal: Xuan's army slackened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's troops faltered.

sentences.zh: 玄感與數千騎乘之，於是大潰，擁八千人而去。

translations.literal: Xuangan with several thousand cavalry charged them, whereupon there was a great rout; he took eight thousand men and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan charged with several thousand horsemen, routing the army; Wei escaped with eight thousand men.

sentences.zh: 玄感驍勇多力，每戰親運長矛，身先士卒，喑鳴叱咤，所當者莫不震攝。

translations.literal: Xuangan was fierce and brave and possessed great strength; in every battle he personally wielded a long spear, took the lead before the soldiers, and with shouts and roars none who faced him failed to be shaken and cowed.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and immensely strong, he fought at the head of his men with a long spear in hand, roaring so that none who faced him failed to quail.

sentences.zh: 論者方之項羽。

translations.literal: Discussants compared him to Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators compared him to Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 又善撫馭，士樂致死，由是戰無不捷。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at comforting and controlling troops; the soldiers gladly gave their lives, and thereby in battle there was none he did not conquer.
translations.idiomatic: He knew how to win men's loyalty, and his soldiers fought gladly to the death; for a time he was unbeaten in the field.

sentences.zh: 玄軍日蹙，糧又盡，乃悉眾決戰，陣於北邙，一日之間，戰十餘合。

translations.literal: Xuan's army was daily pressed tighter, and provisions were also exhausted; he then committed his entire force to a decisive battle, forming ranks on Mount Beimang; within a single day they fought more than ten engagements.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's position grew tighter daily and his supplies ran out; he threw his whole force into a decisive battle on Mount Beimang, fighting more than ten clashes in a single day.

sentences.zh: 玄感弟玄挺中流矢而斃，玄感稍却。

translations.literal: Xuangan's brother Xu Ting was struck by a flying arrow and died; Xuangan withdrew somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan's brother Xu Ting was struck down by an arrow, and Xuangan fell back.

sentences.zh: 樊子蓋復遣兵攻尚書省，又殺數百人。

translations.literal: Fan Zigai again sent troops to attack the Ministry of State Affairs compound, killing several hundred more.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai sent troops against the Ministry compound again and killed several hundred more.

sentences.zh: 帝遣武賁郎將陳稜攻元務本於黎陽，武衞將軍屈突通屯河陽，左翊衞大將軍宇文述發兵繼進，右驍衞大將軍來護兒復來赴援。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Majordomo Chen Ling to attack Yuan Wuben at Liyang, General Qu Tu Tong to encamp at Heyang, Left Guard General Yuwen Shu to set out with troops in succession, and Right Valiant Cavalry General Lai Huer to come again to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Chen Ling against Yuan Wuben at Liyang, posted Qu Tu Tong at Heyang, ordered Yuwen Shu forward in support, and recalled Lai Huer to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 玄感請計於前民部尚書李子雄，子雄曰：「屈突通曉習兵事，若一渡河，則勝負難決，不如分兵拒之。

translations.literal: Xuangan asked counsel of former Minister of Population Li Zixiong; Zixiong said, "Qu Tu Tong is well versed in military affairs; if he crosses the river once, victory and defeat will be hard to decide—better to divide forces and resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan consulted the former Minister of Population Li Zixiong, who said, "Qu Tu Tong knows war. Once he crosses the river, the issue will be in doubt—better to detach troops and block him.

sentences.zh: 通不能濟，則樊、衞失援。」

translations.literal: If Tong cannot cross, then Fan and Wei will lose support.
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot cross, Fan and Wei will be cut off from reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 玄感然之，將拒通。

translations.literal: Xuangan approved this and was about to resist Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan agreed and prepared to block Qu Tu Tong.

sentences.zh: 子蓋知其謀，數擊其營，玄感不果進。

translations.literal: Zigai learned of the plan and repeatedly struck his camp; Xuangan could not carry out the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai learned of the plan and repeatedly attacked his camp, so Xuangan could not move against Qu.

sentences.zh: 通遂濟河，軍於破陵。

translations.literal: Tong thereupon crossed the river and encamped at Poling.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tu Tong crossed the river and encamped at Poling.

sentences.zh: 玄感為兩軍，西抗衞玄，東拒屈突通。

translations.literal: Xuangan formed two armies, resisting Wei Xuan in the west and Qu Tu Tong in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan split his force, facing Wei Xuan in the west and Qu Tu Tong in the east.

sentences.zh: 子蓋復出兵，於是大戰，玄感軍頻北。

translations.literal: Zigai again sent out troops; thereupon a great battle was fought, and Xuangan's army repeatedly retreated north.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai sallied again; in the great battle that followed Xuangan's army was repeatedly driven back.

sentences.zh: 復請計於子雄，子雄曰：「東都援軍益至，我師屢敗，不可久留。

translations.literal: He again asked counsel of Zixiong; Zixiong said, "Relief troops for the Eastern Capital arrive daily in greater numbers, and our army has repeatedly been defeated—we cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: He consulted Li Zixiong again, who said, "Reinforcements pour into the Eastern Capital and we have lost again and again—we cannot remain here.

sentences.zh: 不如直入關中，開永豐倉以賑貧乏，三輔可指麾而定。

translations.literal: Better to drive straight into Guanzhong, open the Yongfeng granary to relieve the poor and destitute, and the Three Adjuncts can be settled with a wave of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike straight into Guanzhong, open the Yongfeng granary to feed the hungry, and the capital region will fall at a gesture.

sentences.zh: 據有府庫，東面而爭天下，此亦霸王之業。」

translations.literal: Possessing the treasuries and arsenals, facing east to contend for the realm—this too is the enterprise of a hegemon king.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the treasuries, turn east, and contend for the empire—that is the path of a hegemon.

sentences.zh: 會華陰諸楊請為鄉導，玄感遂釋洛陽，西圖關中，宣言曰：「我已破東都，取關西矣。」

translations.literal: It happened that the Yang clan of Huayin asked to serve as local guides; Xuangan then released Luoyang and turned west to aim at Guanzhong, proclaiming, "I have already broken the Eastern Capital and am taking Guanxi."
translations.idiomatic: The Yang kin of Huayin offered to guide him, so he abandoned Luoyang and marched west toward Guanzhong, proclaiming, "I have taken the Eastern Capital and now seize the west."

sentences.zh: 宇文述等諸軍躡之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu and the other armies pursued on his heels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu and the other imperial armies pressed close behind.

sentences.zh: 至弘農宮，父老遮說玄感曰：「宮城空虛，又多積粟，攻之易下。

translations.literal: When he reached Hongnong Palace, the elders blocked his way and urged Xuangan, "The palace city is empty and also has much stored grain—attack it and it will easily fall.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongnong Palace the local elders waylaid him and urged, "The palace is lightly held and full of grain—it will fall easily.

sentences.zh: 進可絕敵人之食，退可割宜陽之地。」

translations.literal: Advancing, you can cut off the enemy's food; retreating, you can seize the territory of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Take it and you cut the enemy's supplies; hold it and you command the Yiyang region.

sentences.zh: 玄感以為然，留攻之，三日城不下，追兵遂至。

translations.literal: Xuangan thought this right and stayed to attack it; after three days the city had not fallen, and pursuing troops then arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed and laid siege, but after three days the city still stood and the pursuers caught up.

sentences.zh: 玄感西至閿鄉，上槃豆，布陣亘五十里，與官軍且戰且行，一日三敗。

translations.literal: Xuangan marched west to Wenxiang and ascended Pandou, drawing up battle lines stretching fifty li; with the government army he fought as he marched, suffering three defeats in one day.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west to Wenxiang and took up position on Pandou, his line stretching fifty li; fighting as he retreated, he lost three battles in a single day.

sentences.zh: 復陣於董杜原，諸軍擊之，玄感大敗，獨與十餘騎竄林木間，將奔上洛。

translations.literal: He again formed ranks at Dongdu Plain; the various armies struck him, and Xuangan was greatly defeated; alone with a dozen or so horsemen he fled among the trees and scrub, intending to run to Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: He made a stand at Dongdu Plain, was routed, and fled into the woods with only a dozen horsemen, heading for Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 追騎至，玄感叱之，皆懼而返走。

translations.literal: Pursuing horsemen arrived; Xuangan shouted at them, and all were afraid and turned back in flight.
translations.idiomatic: When pursuers caught up, he roared at them and they fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 至葭蘆戍，玄感窘迫，獨與弟積善步行。

translations.literal: When he reached Jialu Post, Xuangan was in dire straits; alone with his brother Jishan he went on foot.
translations.idiomatic: At Jialu Post, hard pressed, he fled on foot with only his brother Jishan.

sentences.zh: 自知不免，謂積善曰：「事敗矣。

translations.literal: Knowing he could not escape, he said to Jishan, "The affair has failed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing there was no escape, he told Jishan, "All is lost.

sentences.zh: 我不能受人戮辱，汝可殺我。」

translations.literal: I cannot suffer the humiliation of being slaughtered by others—you may kill me.
translations.idiomatic: I will not endure the shame of capture—kill me.

sentences.zh: 積善抽刀斫殺之，因自刺，不死，為追兵所執，與玄感首俱送行在所。

translations.literal: Jishan drew his blade and hacked him to death, then stabbed himself but did not die; he was seized by pursuing troops, and together with Xuangan's head was sent to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jishan struck him down with his sword, then stabbed himself but survived; the pursuers seized him and sent him, with Xuangan's head, to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 磔其屍於東都市三日，復臠而焚之。

translations.literal: His corpse was dismembered and exposed in the Eastern Capital market for three days, then cut to pieces again and burned.
translations.idiomatic: His body was dismembered and displayed in the Eastern Capital market for three days, then cut apart and burned.

sentences.zh: 餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: The remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels were all suppressed.

sentences.zh: 其弟玄奬為義陽太守，將歸玄感，為郡丞周琁玉所殺。

translations.literal: His brother Xu Jiang was regional governor of Yiyang and was about to join Xuangan when he was killed by the commandery aide Zhou Xianyu.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xu Jiang, governor of Yiyang, was marching to join him when the commandery aide Zhou Xianyu killed him.

sentences.zh: 玄縱弟萬碩，自帝所逃歸，至高陽，止傳舍，監事許華與郡兵執之，斬於涿郡。

translations.literal: Xu Zong's brother Wan Shuo fled back from the emperor's presence, reached Gaoyang, and stopped at a relay station; supervisor Xu Hua with commandery troops seized him and beheaded him at Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zong's brother Wan Shuo fled the imperial camp, reached Gaoyang, and lodged at a post station; the supervisor Xu Hua and local troops seized him and executed him at Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 萬碩弟民行，官至朝請大夫，斬於長安。

translations.literal: Wan Shuo's brother Minxing, whose office had reached Court Gentleman for Consultation, was beheaded at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Shuo's brother Minxing, who had risen to Court Gentleman for Consultation, was executed at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 並具梟磔。

translations.literal: All were likewise subjected to dismemberment and exposure.
translations.idiomatic: All were dismembered and put on public display in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 公卿請改玄感姓為梟氏，詔可之。

translations.literal: The high officials asked that Xuangan's surname be changed to the Xiao clan; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court asked that Xuangan's clan name be changed to Xiao, meaning "owl," and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 初，玄感圍東都也，梁郡人韓相國舉兵應之，玄感以為河南道元帥。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital, Han Xiangguo of Liang commandery raised troops in response; Xuangan made him marshal of the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital, Han Xiangguo of Liang commandery rose in support, and Xuangan appointed him marshal of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 旬月間，眾十餘萬，攻剽郡縣。

translations.literal: Within a month or so his forces reached more than a hundred thousand, and he raided commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Within weeks he mustered more than a hundred thousand men and raided the surrounding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 至于襄城，遇玄感敗，兵漸潰散，為吏所執，傳首東都。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiangcheng he encountered Xuangan's defeat; his troops gradually scattered, he was seized by officials, and his head was sent to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangcheng he learned of Xuangan's defeat; his army melted away, he was captured, and his head was sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 李子雄李子雄，渤海蓨人也。

translations.literal: Li Zixiong was a native of Mao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiong was a native of Mao in Bohai commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖伯賁，魏諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bo Ben was Remonstrating and Advising Grand Master of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bo Ben had served Wei as Remonstrating and Advising Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 父桃枝，東平太守，與鄉人高仲密同歸於周，官至冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Taozhi was regional governor of Dongping; with his fellow townsman Gao Zhongmi he submitted to Zhou and rose to regional inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Taozhi, once governor of Dongping, had submitted to Zhou with his townsman Gao Zhongmi and risen to inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子雄少慷慨，有壯志。

translations.literal: Zixiong in youth was openhanded and magnanimous, with a bold ambition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zixiong was generous and high-minded, with a warrior's ambition.

sentences.zh: 弱冠從周武帝平齊，以功授帥都督。

translations.literal: At his capping he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in pacifying Qi and was appointed commander-in-chief by merit.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in the conquest of Qi and was made a commander-in-chief for his service.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，從韋孝寬破尉迥於相州，拜上開府，賜爵建昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu served as Chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yuwen Jiong at Xiangzhou, was appointed Grand Opening Master, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jianchang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was Chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yuwen Jiong at Xiangzhou, was made Grand Opening Master, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，為驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he became General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Zixiong became General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，以功進位大將軍，歷郴、江二州刺史，並有能名。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he was promoted to Great General for merit, served as regional inspector of Chen and Jiang in succession, and in both posts won a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chen campaign he was promoted to Great General, then served as inspector of Chen and Jiang, earning a name for competence in both posts.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒之作亂也，煬帝將發幽州兵以討之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Yang Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang was about to dispatch Youzhou troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Han Yang Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang prepared to mobilize the Youzhou army against him.

sentences.zh: 時竇抗為幽州總管，帝恐其有二心，問可任者於楊素。

translations.literal: At that time Dou Kang was overall commander of Youzhou; the emperor feared he might harbor divided loyalties and asked Yang Su who could be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Kang was overall commander of Youzhou, and the emperor, fearing disloyalty, asked Yang Su whom he could trust.

sentences.zh: 素進子雄，授大將軍，拜廉州刺史，馳至幽州，止傳舍，召募得千餘人。

translations.literal: Su recommended Zixiong; he was appointed Great General and regional inspector of Lianzhou, galloped to Youzhou, stopped at a relay station, and recruited more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Su recommended Zixiong, who was made Great General and inspector of Lianzhou, rode at once to Youzhou, lodged at a post station, and raised more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 抗恃素貴，不時相見。

translations.literal: Kang relied on Su's exalted status and did not come to see him promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Kang, counting on Su's backing, did not come to see him at once.

sentences.zh: 子雄遣人諭之。

translations.literal: Zixiong sent men to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong sent men to summon him.

sentences.zh: 後二日，抗從鐵騎二千，來詣子雄所。

translations.literal: Two days later Kang came with two thousand iron cavalry to Zixiong's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Kang arrived with two thousand armored horsemen.

sentences.zh: 子雄伏甲，請與相見，因擒抗。

translations.literal: Zixiong had hidden armor, invited him to a meeting, and thereupon seized Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong had laid an ambush, received him for a meeting, and seized him.

sentences.zh: 遂發幽州兵步騎三萬，自井陘以討諒。

translations.literal: He then dispatched thirty thousand infantry and cavalry of the Youzhou army through Jingxing Pass to attack Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched thirty thousand Youzhou foot and horse through Jingxing Pass against Liang.

sentences.zh: 時諒遣大將軍劉建略地燕、趙，正攻井陘，相遇於抱犢山下，力戰，破之。

translations.literal: At that time Liang had sent Great General Liu Jian to seize territory in Yan and Zhao and was attacking Jingxing; they met below Mount Baodu, fought fiercely, and he defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had sent Liu Jian to overrun Yan and Zhao and was attacking Jingxing; they met below Mount Baodu, fought hard, and Zixiong routed him.

sentences.zh: 遷幽州總管，尋徵拜民部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to overall commander of Youzhou and soon summoned and appointed Minister of Population.
translations.idiomatic: He was made overall commander of Youzhou, then recalled as Minister of Population.

sentences.zh: 子雄明辯有器幹，帝甚任之。

translations.literal: Zixiong was clear in debate and possessed capacity and backbone; the emperor greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-minded and capable, he enjoyed the emperor's strong trust.

sentences.zh: 新羅嘗遣使朝貢，子雄至朝堂與語，因問其冠制所由。

translations.literal: Silla once sent envoys to offer tribute; Zixiong went to the court hall to speak with them and asked the origin of their headgear.
translations.idiomatic: When Silla sent tribute envoys, Zixiong met them in court and asked about the origin of their caps.

sentences.zh: 其使者曰：「皮弁遺象。

translations.literal: The envoy said, "The leather cap preserves the image.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy replied, "It preserves the form of the leather cap.

sentences.zh: 安有大國君子而不識皮弁也！」

translations.literal: How can there be a gentleman of a great state who does not recognize the leather cap!
translations.idiomatic: What gentleman of a great kingdom does not know the leather cap!

sentences.zh: 子雄因曰：「中國無禮，求諸四夷。」

translations.literal: Zixiong thereupon said, "The Middle Kingdom has lost ritual—one must seek it among the four barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong retorted, "China has lost its rites and must seek them among the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「自至已來，此言之外，未見無禮。」

translations.literal: The envoy said, "Since arriving, apart from this remark, I have seen no lack of ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy answered, "Since I arrived, apart from that remark, I have seen no discourtesy."

sentences.zh: 憲司以子雄失詞，奏劾其事，竟坐免。

translations.literal: The censorate, on the grounds that Zixiong had misspoken, memorialized to impeach the matter, and in the end he was dismissed for it.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate impeached him for the gaffe, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 俄而復職，從幸江都。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored to office and followed the emperor on the journey to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored and accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 帝以仗衞不整，顧子雄部伍之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the guard of arms was not in order, turned to Zixiong to array the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial guard fell into disorder, the emperor had Zixiong put the ranks in order.

sentences.zh: 子雄立指麾，六軍肅然。

translations.literal: Zixiong stood directing commands, and the six armies became sternly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong took command on the spot, and the whole army fell into perfect order.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅曰：「公真武候才也。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said, "Your Excellency truly has the talent of a martial guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and said, "You truly have the makings of a guard commander.

sentences.zh: 尋轉右武候大將軍，後坐事除名。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Martial Guard General; later he was struck from the rolls for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Right Martial Guard General, but later was struck from the rolls for an offense.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，帝令從軍自效，因從來護兒自東平將指滄海。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign the emperor ordered him to follow the army and prove himself, and he therefore followed Lai Huer from Dongping, intending to point toward the blue sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign the emperor ordered him to redeem himself in the ranks, and he followed Lai Huer from Dongping toward the sea.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感反於黎陽，帝疑之，詔鎖子雄送行在所。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled at Liyang the emperor suspected him and ordered Zixiong shackled and sent to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled at Liyang the emperor grew suspicious and ordered Zixiong shackled and brought to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 子雄殺使者，亡歸玄感。

translations.literal: Zixiong killed the envoy and fled back to Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong killed the escort and fled to Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 玄感每請計於子雄，語在玄感傳。

translations.literal: Xuangan often asked Zixiong for counsel; the account is in Xuangan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan often sought his counsel, as recounted in Xuangan's biography.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗，伏誅，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was defeated, he was executed, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan fell, Zixiong was executed and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 趙元淑博陵趙元淑，父世模，初事高寶寧，後以眾歸周，授上開府，寓居京兆之雲陽。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuanshu of Boling—his father Shimao at first served Gao Baoning, later submitted to Zhou with his followers, was appointed Grand Opening Master, and resided at Yunyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuanshu of Boling—his father Shimao had first served Gao Baoning, then brought his followers to Zhou, was made Grand Opening Master, and settled at Yunyang in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，恒典宿衞。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he constantly supervised the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Shimao served permanently in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 後從晉王伐陳，先鋒遇賊，力戰而死。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Prince of Jin in attacking Chen; the vanguard met the enemy, fought fiercely, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the Prince of Jin against Chen; in the vanguard he met the enemy, fought hard, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其身死王事，以元淑襲父本官，賜物二千段。

translations.literal: The court, because he had died in the king's service, had Yuanshu inherit his father's original office and bestowed two thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had died in the prince's service, the court let Yuanshu inherit his father's post and gave him two thousand lengths of silk.

sentences.zh: 元淑性疎誕，不治產業，家徒壁立。

translations.literal: Yuanshu was by nature careless and unrestrained, did not manage his estate, and his household was bare as the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshu was careless and improvident, kept no estate, and lived in bare poverty.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，授驃騎將軍，將之官，無以自給。

translations.literal: Several years later he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry; about to take up his post, he had no means to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was made General of Agile Cavalry, but on the eve of taking office he had nothing to live on.

sentences.zh: 時長安富人宗連，家累千金，仕周為三原令。

translations.literal: At that time the wealthy man of Chang'an Zong Lian had a household accumulating a thousand in gold and had served Zhou as magistrate of Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy Chang'an man named Zong Lian, worth a thousand in gold, had served Zhou as magistrate of Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 有季女，慧而有色，連獨奇之，每求賢夫。

translations.literal: He had a youngest daughter, clever and beautiful; Lian alone prized her and constantly sought a worthy husband.
translations.idiomatic: He had a youngest daughter, clever and beautiful, whom he cherished and for whom he always sought a worthy husband.

sentences.zh: 聞元淑如是，請與相見。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yuanshu was such a man, he asked to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Yuanshu, he asked to meet him.

sentences.zh: 連有風儀，美談笑，元淑亦異之。

translations.literal: Lian had bearing and grace and was skilled in conversation and laughter; Yuanshu also found him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was dignified and witty, and Yuanshu was impressed.

sentences.zh: 及至其家，服玩居處擬於將相。

translations.literal: When he reached his home, clothing, ornaments, and dwelling rivaled those of generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At Lian's house, furnishings and quarters rivaled those of a general or minister.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，奏女樂，元淑所未見也。

translations.literal: When the wine was warm they performed women's music—something Yuanshu had never seen.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was flowing, female musicians performed—splendor Yuanshu had never known.

sentences.zh: 元淑辭出，連曰：「公子有暇，可復來也。」

translations.literal: Yuanshu took leave; Lian said, "When the young lord has leisure, you may come again.
translations.idiomatic: As Yuanshu left, Lian said, "Come again when you have time, my lord.

sentences.zh: 後數日，復造之，宴樂更侈。

translations.literal: Several days later he visited again, and the feast and music were even more lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he returned, and the entertainment was even grander.

sentences.zh: 如此者再三，因謂元淑曰：「知公子素貧，老夫當相濟。」

translations.literal: This happened three or four times; he then said to Yuanshu, "Knowing that the young lord has long been poor, this old man ought to help you.
translations.idiomatic: After several such visits Lian told him, "I know you have been poor; let me help you.

sentences.zh: 因問元淑所須，盡買與之。

translations.literal: He then asked what Yuanshu needed and bought everything for him.
translations.idiomatic: He asked what Yuanshu needed and bought it all for him.

sentences.zh: 臨別，元淑再拜致謝，連復拜曰：「鄙人竊不自量，敬慕公子。

translations.literal: On parting Yuanshu bowed twice in thanks; Lian bowed again and said, "This humble man presumptuously failed to measure himself and reveres and admires the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: As Yuanshu bowed his thanks, Lian bowed in return and said, "Forgive my presumption—I have long admired you, my lord.

sentences.zh: 今有一女，願為箕帚妾，公子意何如？」

translations.literal: I now have a daughter who wishes to become a broom-and-dustpan concubine—what does the young lord think?
translations.idiomatic: I have a daughter who would be honored to serve you as wife—what do you say?

sentences.zh: 元淑感愧，遂娉為妻。

translations.literal: Yuanshu was moved and ashamed and thereupon betrothed her as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Moved and ashamed, Yuanshu took her as his wife.

sentences.zh: 連復送奴婢二十口、良馬十餘匹，加以縑帛錦綺及金寶珍玩。

translations.literal: Lian again sent twenty household slaves and more than ten fine horses, together with silks, brocades, gold, jewels, and precious curios.
translations.idiomatic: Lian also gave him twenty servants, more than ten fine horses, silks and brocades, and gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 元淑遂為富人。

translations.literal: Yuanshu thereby became a rich man.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshu was suddenly a wealthy man.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，漢王諒作亂，元淑從楊素擊平之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Prince of Han Yang Liang rebelled; Yuanshu followed Yang Su in striking and pacifying him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Prince of Han Yang Liang rebelled, and Yuanshu followed Yang Su to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 以功進位柱國，拜德州刺史，尋轉潁川太守，並有威惠。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Pillar of State, appointed regional inspector of Dezhou, and soon transferred to grand administrator of Yingchuan; in both posts he had authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Pillar of State, then inspector of Dezhou and soon grand administrator of Yingchuan, winning respect in both posts.

sentences.zh: 因入朝，會司農不時納諸郡租穀，元淑奏之。

translations.literal: When he came to court it happened that the Director of Agriculture was not receiving the rent grain of the commanderies on time; Yuanshu memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to court he reported that the Director of Agriculture was failing to collect the grain taxes on schedule.

sentences.zh: 帝謂元淑曰：「如卿意者，幾日當了？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yuanshu, "In your opinion, how many days would it take to finish?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked him, "How long would it take, in your view?

sentences.zh: 元淑曰：「如臣意不過十日。」

translations.literal: Yuanshu said, "In this servant's opinion, no more than ten days."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshu said, "No more than ten days, in my judgment."

sentences.zh: 帝即日拜元淑為司農卿，納天下租，如言而了。

translations.literal: The emperor that same day appointed Yuanshu Director of Agriculture; he collected the realm's rents and finished as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed him Director of Agriculture that same day; he collected the empire's rents and finished within ten days as promised.

sentences.zh: 帝悅焉。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書楊玄感潛有異志，以元淑可與共亂，遂與結交，多遺金寶。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan secretly harbored divergent ambitions; considering that Yuanshu could join him in disorder, he formed a bond with him and sent him many gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan secretly plotted rebellion and, thinking Yuanshu a useful ally, befriended him and sent him lavish gifts of gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，領將軍，典宿衞，加授光祿大夫，封葛公。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he led as general, supervised the night guard, was additionally appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ge.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he served as a leading general, commanded the palace guard, was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ge.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復征高麗，以元淑鎮臨渝。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor again campaigned against Goryeo and stationed Yuanshu at Linyu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on another campaign against Goryeo, the emperor posted Yuanshu at Linyu.

sentences.zh: 及玄感作亂，其弟玄縱自帝所逃歸，路經臨渝。

translations.literal: When Xuangan rebelled, his brother Xu Zong fled back from the emperor's presence and passed by Linyu on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan rebelled, his brother Xu Zong fled the imperial camp and passed through Linyu.

sentences.zh: 元淑出其小妻魏氏見玄縱，對宴極歡，因與通謀，并授玄縱賂遺。

translations.literal: Yuanshu brought out his junior wife Lady Wei to meet Xu Zong; they feasted together in the greatest joy and thereupon entered into conspiracy, also presenting Xu Zong with bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshu introduced his concubine Lady Wei, feasted Xu Zong lavishly, conspired with him, and gave him gifts for the road.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗，人有告其事者，帝以屬吏。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was defeated, someone reported the affair, and the emperor handed him over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuangan's defeat someone informed on him, and the emperor turned the case over to the judges.

sentences.zh: 元淑言與玄感結婚，所得金寶則為財娉，實無他故。

translations.literal: Yuanshu said he had formed a marriage bond with Xuangan and that the gold and jewels received were betrothal gifts, with no other cause in fact.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshu claimed he had married into Xuangan's family and that the gold was merely betrothal gifts, with no treasonous intent.

sentences.zh: 魏氏復言初不受金。

translations.literal: Lady Wei again said she had at first not accepted gold.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei likewise denied ever accepting gold.

sentences.zh: 帝親臨問，卒無異辭。

translations.literal: The emperor personally came to question them; in the end there was no change in their statements.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned them in person, but their stories never changed.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，謂侍臣曰：「此則反狀，何勞重問！」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and said to his attendants, "This is plainly the form of rebellion—why trouble to question again!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and told his attendants, "This is open treason—why question them further!

sentences.zh: 元淑及魏氏俱斬於涿郡，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Yuanshu and Lady Wei were both beheaded at Zhuo commandery, and their household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshu and Lady Wei were beheaded at Zhuo, and their property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 斛斯政河南斛斯政，祖椿，魏太保、尚書令、常山文宣王；

translations.literal: Hu Shizheng of Henan—his grandfather Chun was Grand Tutor of Wei, Minister of State Affairs, and Prince Wenxuan of Changshan;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shizheng of Henan—his grandfather Chun had been Wei Grand Tutor, Minister of State Affairs, and Prince Wenxuan of Changshan;

sentences.zh: 父恢，散騎常侍、新蔡郡公。

translations.literal: his father Hui was Regular Attendant and Duke of Xincai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: his father Hui, Regular Attendant and Duke of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 政明悟有器幹，初為親衞，後以軍功授儀同，甚為楊素所禮。

translations.literal: Shizheng was perceptive and possessed capacity and backbone; at first he was in the personal guard, later received the rank of Peer for military merit, and was greatly honored by Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng was clever and capable; he began in the personal guard, won the rank of Peer for military merit, and was highly regarded by Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為尚書兵曹郎。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was Secretary of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he served as Secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 政有風神，每奏事，未嘗不稱旨。

translations.literal: Shizheng had spirit and bearing; each time he reported affairs he never failed to accord with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He had presence and grace, and every report he made pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 煬帝悅之，漸見委信。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was pleased with him and gradually entrusted him with confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang took a liking to him and gradually came to trust him.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感兄弟俱與之交。

translations.literal: The brothers Yang Xuangan all formed friendships with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Yang Xuangan and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，兵部尚書段文振卒，侍郎明雅復以罪廢，帝彌屬意。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign Minister of War Duan Wenzhen died, and Vice Minister Ming Ya was again dismissed for an offense; the emperor increasingly fixed his intent on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign Minister of War Duan Wenzhen died and Vice Minister Ming Ya was dismissed; the emperor turned increasingly to Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 尋遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 于時外事四夷，軍國多務，政處斷辯速，稱為幹理。

translations.literal: At that time foreign affairs involved the four barbarians and military and state affairs were many; Shizheng's decisions were swift in debate and he was called capable in administration.
translations.idiomatic: With frontier troubles on every side and the state overwhelmed with business, he decided cases swiftly and was praised for his efficiency.

sentences.zh: 玄感之反也，政與通謀。

translations.literal: When Xuangan rebelled, Shizheng entered into conspiracy with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan rebelled, Shizheng conspired with him.

sentences.zh: 及玄縱等亡歸，亦政之計也。

translations.literal: When Xu Zong and the others fled back, that too was Shizheng's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The flight of Xu Zong and the others was also his doing.

sentences.zh: 帝在遼東，將班師，窮治玄縱黨與。

translations.literal: The emperor was in Liaodong and was about to withdraw the army; he thoroughly investigated Xu Zong's associates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in Liaodong preparing to withdraw and was hunting down Xu Zong's accomplices.

sentences.zh: 內不自安，遂亡奔高麗。

translations.literal: Inwardly ill at ease, he thereupon fled to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear the pressure, he fled to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復東征，高麗請降，求執送政。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor again campaigned east; Goryeo requested surrender and asked to seize and deliver Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on another eastern campaign, Goryeo offered surrender and agreed to hand Shizheng over.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，遂鎖政而還。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this and thereupon had Shizheng shackled and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Shizheng was brought back in chains.

sentences.zh: 至京師，以政告廟，左翊衞大將軍宇文述奏曰：「斛斯政之罪，天地所不容，人神所同忿。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he reported Shizheng to the ancestral temple; Left Guard General Yuwen Shu memorialized, saying, "Hu Shizheng's crime is what Heaven and Earth cannot tolerate and what men and spirits alike resent.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital he was reported to the ancestral temple. Left Guard General Yuwen Shu memorialized, "Hu Shizheng's crime outrages Heaven and Earth and stirs the wrath of gods and men alike.

sentences.zh: 若同常刑，賊臣逆子何以懲肅，請變常法。」

translations.literal: If he receives the usual punishment, how are treacherous ministers and rebellious sons to be disciplined and awed— I request a change from the usual law.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary punishment will not suffice to warn traitors—I beg that the law be set aside.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 於是將政出金光門，縛政於柱，公卿百僚並親擊射，臠割其肉，多有噉者。

translations.literal: Thereupon they led Shizheng out through the Golden Light Gate, bound him to a pillar, and the high officials and hundred ranks all personally shot at him, cut his flesh in pieces, and many ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng was led out through the Golden Light Gate, bound to a post, and the whole court shot at him, cut his flesh, and many ate it.

sentences.zh: 噉後烹煮，收其餘骨，焚而揚之。

translations.literal: After they had eaten, they boiled him; they gathered his remaining bones, burned them, and scattered the ashes.
translations.idiomatic: When they had finished eating his flesh, they boiled what remained, collected the bones, burned them, and cast the ashes to the wind.

sentences.zh: 劉元進餘杭劉元進，少好任俠，為州里所宗。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjin — Liu Yuanjin of Yuhang — in youth loved chivalrous daring and was honored by his district.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjin of Yuhang. From youth he loved bold, chivalrous deeds, and his district looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 兩手各長尺餘，臂垂過膝。

translations.literal: Each hand was more than a foot long, and his arms hung down past his knees.
translations.idiomatic: Each of his hands measured more than a foot in length, and his arms reached below his knees.

sentences.zh: 煬帝興遼東之役，百姓騷動，元進自以相表非常，陰有異志，遂聚眾，合亡命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang raised the Liaodong campaign, the common people were in turmoil; Yuanjin considered his physiognomy extraordinary, harbored divergent ambitions in secret, and thereupon gathered a host and joined with fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang launched the Liaodong campaigns, the people were in uproar. Yuanjin believed his features marked him for greatness and secretly nursed rebellious designs; he gathered followers and took in outlaws.

sentences.zh: 會帝復征遼東，徵兵吳、會，士卒皆相謂曰：「去年吾輩父兄從帝征者，當全盛之時，猶死亡太半，骸骨不歸；

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor again campaigned against Liaodong and drafted troops from Wu and Kuaiji; the soldiers all said to one another, "Last year our fathers and elder brothers who followed the emperor on campaign — even at the height of our strength, more than half still died, and their bones did not return home;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor again marched on Liaodong and conscripted men from Wu and Kuaiji, the soldiers said among themselves: "Last year our fathers and brothers followed the emperor east—even at the empire's height, more than half died, and their bones never came home;

sentences.zh: 今天下已罷敝，是行也，吾屬其無遺類矣。」

translations.literal: Now the realm is already exhausted — on this expedition, none of us will be left alive.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is spent. On this march, not one of us will survive.

sentences.zh: 於是多有亡散，郡縣捕之急。

translations.literal: Thereupon many fled and scattered, and the districts and counties hunted them down urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Many fled and scattered, and the local authorities hunted them down without mercy.

sentences.zh: 既而楊玄感起於黎陽，元進知天下思亂，於是舉兵應之。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Xuangan rose at Liyang; Yuanjin knew the realm yearned for turmoil, and thereupon raised troops to answer him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled at Liyang, Yuanjin saw that the empire was ripe for revolt and raised his own forces in support.

sentences.zh: 三吳苦役者莫不響至，旬月眾至數萬。

translations.literal: Hard-pressed laborers of the Three Wu regions none failed to respond and come; within a month and ten days his host reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers oppressed throughout the Three Wu flocked to him, and within a month his following swelled to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 將渡江，而玄感敗。

translations.literal: He was about to cross the Yangzi when Xuangan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the point of crossing the Yangzi when Xuangan's rebellion collapsed.

sentences.zh: 吳郡朱爕、晉陵管崇亦舉兵，有眾七萬，共迎元進，奉以為主。

translations.literal: Zhu Can of Wu commandery and Guan Chong of Jinling also raised troops; they had a host of seventy thousand, jointly welcomed Yuanjin, and made him their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinling also took up arms. With seventy thousand men they welcomed Yuanjin and installed him as their chief.

sentences.zh: 據吳郡，稱天子，爕、崇俱為僕射，署置百官。

translations.literal: They occupied Wu commandery, styled themselves Son of Heaven, made Can and Chong both Vice Ministers, and appointed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Wu commandery, Yuanjin declared himself emperor, and Can and Chong were both made Vice Ministers as a full court was appointed.

sentences.zh: 毗陵、東陽、會稽、建安豪傑多執長吏以應之。

translations.literal: Notables of Piling, Dongyang, Kuaiji, and Jian'an mostly seized their chief administrators to answer them.
translations.idiomatic: Local leaders across Piling, Dongyang, Kuaiji, and Jian'an seized their magistrates and rallied to the cause.

sentences.zh: 帝令將軍吐萬緒、光祿大夫魚俱羅率兵討焉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered General Tuwán Xù and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Yu Juluo to lead troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched General Tuwán Xù and Grand Master Yu Juluo to crush them.

sentences.zh: 元進西屯茅浦，以抗官軍，頻戰互有勝負。

translations.literal: Yuanjin encamped west at Maopu to resist the government armies; they fought repeatedly with alternating victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin encamped at Maopu on the west to block the imperial forces, and in repeated clashes each side claimed victories.

sentences.zh: 元進退保曲阿，與朱爕、管崇合軍，眾至十萬。

translations.literal: Yuanjin withdrew to defend Qu'e, united armies with Zhu Can and Guan Chong, and their host reached one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin fell back on Qu'e, joined Zhu Can and Guan Chong, and their combined strength rose to one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 緒進軍逼之，相持百餘日，為緒所敗，保於黃山。

translations.literal: Xù advanced his army to press them; they held each other off for more than a hundred days; he was defeated by Xù and took refuge on Mount Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Xù pressed the attack, and after more than a hundred days of stalemate Yuanjin was beaten back and took refuge on Mount Huang.

sentences.zh: 緒復破之，爕戰死，元進引趣建安，休兵養士。

translations.literal: Xù again defeated him; Can died in battle; Yuanjin led his forces toward Jian'an and rested the army to nourish the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xù defeated him again. Can fell in battle. Yuanjin withdrew toward Jian'an to regroup and restore his men's strength.

sentences.zh: 二將亦以師老，頓軍自守。

translations.literal: The two generals also, because their armies were weary, halted their troops and held themselves on the defensive.
translations.idiomatic: The two imperial generals, their troops worn out, halted and held their positions.

sentences.zh: 俄而二將俱得罪，帝令江都郡丞王世充發淮南兵擊之。

translations.literal: Before long both generals fell afoul of the throne; the emperor ordered Jiangdu District Assistant Wang Shichong to raise Huainan troops and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both generals fell from favor, and the emperor ordered Wang Shichong, assistant magistrate of Jiangdu, to lead Huainan forces against Yuanjin.

sentences.zh: 有大流星墜於江都，未及地而南逝，磨拂竹木皆有聲，至吳郡而落于地。

translations.literal: A great meteor fell at Jiangdu; before reaching the ground it sped southward, brushing bamboo and trees so that all gave sound; it reached Wu commandery and then fell to earth.
translations.idiomatic: A great meteor fell toward Jiangdu. Before it touched the ground it veered south, tearing through bamboo groves with a roar, and only struck earth when it reached Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 元進惡之，令掘地，入二丈，得一石，徑丈餘。

translations.literal: Yuanjin regarded it as ill-omened and ordered the ground dug; at two zhang down they obtained a stone more than one zhang in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin took it as an evil omen and had the ground excavated. At a depth of two zhang they found a stone more than ten feet across.

sentences.zh: 後數日，失石所在。

translations.literal: Several days later the stone's whereabouts were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the stone had vanished.

sentences.zh: 世充既渡江，元進將兵拒戰，殺千餘人。

translations.literal: After Shichong had crossed the Yangzi, Yuanjin led troops to oppose him in battle and killed more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shichong had crossed the Yangzi, Yuanjin met him in battle and killed more than a thousand of his men.

sentences.zh: 世充窘急，退保延陵柵。

translations.literal: Shichong was hard pressed and withdrew to hold the palisade at Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong was driven to extremity and pulled back into the stockade at Yanling.

sentences.zh: 元進遺兵，人各持茅，因風縱火。

translations.literal: Yuanjin sent out troops; each man held straw and, taking advantage of the wind, set fires.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin sent his men forward, each carrying bundles of straw, and set fires before the wind.

sentences.zh: 世充大懼，將棄營而遁。

translations.literal: Shichong was greatly afraid and was about to abandon the camp and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong was terrified and prepared to abandon his camp and flee.

sentences.zh: 遇反風，火轉，元進之眾懼燒而退。

translations.literal: They met a contrary wind; the fire turned back, and Yuanjin's host, fearing being burned, retreated.
translations.idiomatic: A wind shift drove the flames back on Yuanjin's army, which broke off in fear of being consumed.

sentences.zh: 世充簡銳卒掩擊，大破之，殺傷太半，自是頻戰輒敗。

translations.literal: Shichong selected crack troops for a surprise assault and routed them utterly, killing and wounding more than half; from then on, whenever they fought he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong picked elite troops for a surprise attack and shattered them, killing or wounding more than half. From then on Yuanjin lost every battle.

sentences.zh: 元進謂管崇曰：「事急矣，當以死決之。」

translations.literal: Yuanjin said to Guan Chong, "The affair is desperate — we must settle it with our lives.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin told Guan Chong, "Matters are desperate. We must stake our lives on one final clash.

sentences.zh: 於是出挑戰，俱為世充所殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon they went out to offer battle and were both killed by Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: They rode out to give battle and were both slain by Shichong.

sentences.zh: 其眾悉降，世充坑之於黃亭澗，死者三萬人。

translations.literal: His host all surrendered; Shichong buried them alive at Huangting Brook — thirty thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: His followers surrendered en masse. Shichong had thirty thousand of them buried alive at Huangting Brook.

sentences.zh: 其餘黨往往保險為盜。

translations.literal: The rest of his partisans often held to difficult terrain and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels scattered to rough country and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 其後董道冲、沈法興、李子通等乘此而起，戰爭不息，逮於隋亡。

translations.literal: Afterward Dong Daochong, Shen Faxing, Li Zitong, and others seized this opportunity to rise; warfare did not cease until the Sui perished.
translations.idiomatic: In their wake Dong Daochong, Shen Faxing, Li Zitong, and others rose in turn, and war raged on until the fall of Sui.

sentences.zh: 李密李密字法主，真鄉公衍之從孫也。

translations.literal: Li Mi — Li Mi, style name Fazhu, was a great-grandson by a collateral line of Duke of Zhenxiang, Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, courtesy name Fazhu, was a collateral descendant of Yan, Duke of Zhenxiang.

sentences.zh: 祖耀，周邢國公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yao was Duke of Xingguo under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yao had been Duke of Xing under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父寬，驍勇善戰，幹略過人，自周及隋，數經將領，至柱國、蒲山郡公，號為名將。

translations.literal: His father Kuan was fierce and brave, skilled in battle, with strategic talent surpassing others; from Zhou through Sui he repeatedly held command, reaching Pillar of State and Duke of Pushan commandery, and was called a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuan was a fierce, capable commander whose strategic gifts set him apart. From Zhou through Sui he held repeated commands, rising to Pillar of State and Duke of Pushan, and was accounted one of the age's great generals.

sentences.zh: 密多籌算，才兼文武，志氣雄遠，常以濟物為己任。

translations.literal: Mi was skilled in planning and calculation, talented in both civil and military arts, with lofty ambition and distant reach; he constantly took relieving the world's needs as his personal charge.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was a master strategist, accomplished in both letters and arms, with far-reaching vision; he made it his life's work to redeem the realm.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，襲父爵蒲山公，乃散家產，賙贍親故，養客禮賢，無所愛吝。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he inherited his father's title Duke of Pushan; thereupon he dispersed his family property, relieved and supported kin and old friends, entertained guests and honored the worthy, and was sparing of nothing he loved.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang he inherited his father's title of Duke of Pushan, then gave away his family wealth to support kin and friends, drew talented men to his house, and held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 與楊玄感為刎頸之交。

translations.literal: With Yang Xuangan he was a friendship to cut the throat — sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yang Xuangan were sworn friends as close as brothers.

sentences.zh: 後更折節，下帷耽學，尤好兵書，誦皆在口。

translations.literal: Later he further restrained his manner, drew the curtain and applied himself to study, especially loved military books, and could recite them all by heart.
translations.idiomatic: Later he disciplined himself, secluded himself in study, devoted himself above all to military classics, and knew them by heart.

sentences.zh: 師事國子助教包愷，受史記、漢書，勵精忘倦，愷門徒皆出其下。

translations.literal: He took as teacher the Guozijian assistant instructor Bao Kai, studied the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han, exerted his spirit without tiring, and all Kai's disciples were below him.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Bao Kai of the Imperial Academy, mastering the Shiji and Hanshu with tireless zeal until he surpassed every fellow student.

sentences.zh: 大業初，授親衞大都督，非其所好，稱疾而歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Chief Commander of the Personal Guard; it was not to his liking, and he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye he was appointed chief commander of the personal guard, a post he disdained; he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 及楊玄感在黎陽，有逆謀，陰遣家僮至京師召密，令與弟玄挺等同赴黎陽。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan was at Liyang with treasonous designs, he secretly sent a household servant to the capital to summon Mi and ordered him to go with his younger brother Xuanting and the others to Liyang together.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan was at Liyang plotting rebellion, he secretly sent a servant to the capital to summon Mi and his brother Xuanting to join him there.

sentences.zh: 玄感舉兵而密至，玄感大喜，以為謀主。

translations.literal: Xuangan raised troops and Mi arrived; Xuangan was greatly pleased and made him chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan rose in arms and Mi arrived, Xuangan was overjoyed and made him his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 玄感謀計於密，密曰：「愚有三計，惟公所擇。

translations.literal: Xuangan consulted Mi on strategy; Mi said, "Your servant has three plans — only you may choose among them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan asked Mi for counsel. Mi said, "I have three plans. The choice is yours.

sentences.zh: 今天子出征，遠在遼外，地去幽州，懸隔千里。

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven is on campaign, far in the eastern Liao wilderness; the ground from here to Youzhou is separated by a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is on campaign far beyond the Liao frontier, a thousand li from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 南有巨海之限，北有胡戎之患，中間一道，理極艱危。

translations.literal: To the south is the barrier of the great sea; to the north the trouble of Hu and Rong tribes; along the single middle road the situation is by nature extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lies the sea; to the north, barbarian raiders; between them a single route—the most perilous ground imaginable.

sentences.zh: 今公擁兵，出其不意，長驅入薊，直扼其喉。

translations.literal: Now if you hold troops and strike where they do not expect, drive straight into Ji and seize them by the throat.
translations.idiomatic: If you march now by surprise straight on Ji, you seize them by the throat.

sentences.zh: 前有高麗，退無歸路，不過旬月，齎糧必盡。

translations.literal: Before you is Goryeo; behind, no road of return; within no more than ten days and a month their carried provisions must be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo lies ahead; retreat is cut off. Within a month their supplies will fail.

sentences.zh: 舉麾一召，其眾自降，不戰而擒，此計之上也。

translations.literal: Raise the pennon with one summons and their host will surrender of itself — capture without battle; this is the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: Raise your banner and they will surrender without a fight. That is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 又關中四塞，天府之國，有衞文昇，不足為意。

translations.literal: Again, the Guanzhong region has four passes for defense — a land of Heaven's treasury — and there is only Wei Wensheng; he is not worth taking into account.
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively, Guanzhong is the empire's fortress, defended on four sides. Wei Wensheng alone is no concern.

sentences.zh: 今宜率眾，經城勿攻，輕齎鼓行，務早西入。

translations.literal: Now you should lead the host, pass cities without attacking, travel light with drums beating, and strive to enter west early.
translations.idiomatic: Lead your men west, bypassing walled cities without siege, traveling light and fast.

sentences.zh: 天子雖還，失其襟帶，據險臨之，故當必剋，萬全之勢，此計之中也。

translations.literal: Though the Son of Heaven returns, having lost the collar and belt of the realm you hold the dangerous terrain and overlook them — therefore you will surely prevail; a posture of complete security — this is the middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the emperor returns, without the heartland you hold the passes above him and cannot fail. That is the sound plan.

sentences.zh: 若隨近逐便，先向東都，唐禕告之，理當固守。
