translations.literal: If you follow what is near and seize convenience, first heading for the Eastern Capital — Tang Yi will report it, and by principle they ought to hold fast in defense.
translations.idiomatic: If you strike east toward Luoyang as convenience dictates, Tang Yi will warn them, and they will rightly hold firm.

sentences.zh: 引兵攻戰，必延歲月，勝負殊未可知，此計之下也。」

translations.literal: Leading troops to attack and fight will surely prolong the months; victory and defeat are altogether uncertain — this is the lower plan.
translations.idiomatic: A siege will drag on for months with no certainty of victory. That is the worst course.

sentences.zh: 玄感曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Xuangan said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan said, "No.

sentences.zh: 公之下計，乃上策矣。

translations.literal: Your lower plan is in fact the upper strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Your worst plan is my best strategy.

sentences.zh: 今百官家口並在東都，若不取之，安能動物？

translations.literal: Now the households of the hundred officials are all at the Eastern Capital — if you do not take it, how can you sway men's hearts?
translations.idiomatic: The families of the whole court are in Luoyang. Without seizing it, how can we win men's loyalty?

sentences.zh: 且經城不拔，何以示威？」

translations.literal: Moreover, if you pass a walled city without taking it, how will you display your might?"
translations.idiomatic: And if we bypass a city without capturing it, where is our terror?"

sentences.zh: 密計遂不行。

translations.literal: Mi's plans thereupon were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 玄感既至東都，皆捷，自謂天下響應，功在朝夕。

translations.literal: After Xuangan reached the Eastern Capital all was victory; he deemed himself answered by the realm and that success lay within days.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuangan reached Luoyang he won every encounter and believed the empire would rally to him and victory was days away.

sentences.zh: 及獲韋福嗣，又委以腹心，是以軍旅之事，不專歸密。

translations.literal: When he captured Wei Fusi he again entrusted him as confidant, so that military affairs no longer rested solely with Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When he captured Wei Fusi he took him into his inner circle, and military decisions no longer belonged to Mi alone.

sentences.zh: 福嗣既非同謀，因戰被執，每設籌畫，皆持兩端。

translations.literal: Fusi was not originally a fellow plotter; seized in battle, whenever he offered plans he held to both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Fusi had never been part of the plot; captured in battle, he hedged every counsel he gave.

sentences.zh: 後使作檄文，福嗣固辭不肯。

translations.literal: Later they had him compose a proclamation; Fusi firmly refused and would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When they ordered him to draft a manifesto, he refused outright.

sentences.zh: 密揣知其情，因謂玄感曰：「福嗣元非同盟，實懷觀望。

translations.literal: Mi surmised his true disposition and therefore said to Xuangan, "Fusi was never originally an ally; he truly harbors watchful waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Mi read his intentions and told Xuangan, "Fusi was never one of us. He waits to see which way fortune turns.

sentences.zh: 明公初起大事，而姦人在側，聽其是非，必為所誤矣。

translations.literal: When you, my lord, have just launched a great undertaking and a treacherous man is at your side, if you heed his rights and wrongs you will surely be misled by him.
translations.idiomatic: You have only just raised this great cause, yet a traitor stands at your ear. Heed his advice and you are undone.

sentences.zh: 請斬謝眾，方可安輯。」

translations.literal: I beg that you behead him to answer the host — only then can things be settled and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off his head before the army, and only then can you command loyalty.

sentences.zh: 玄感曰：「何至於此！」

translations.literal: Xuangan said, "How could it come to that!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan said, "Surely not to that!"

sentences.zh: 密知言之不用，退謂所親曰：「楚公好反而不欲勝，如何？

translations.literal: Mi knew his words would not be used; withdrawing he said to those close to him, "The Duke of Chu loves turning back yet does not wish to win — what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Mi knew he had been dismissed. To his intimates he said, "The Duke of Chu toys with defeat yet will not seize victory—what are we to do?

sentences.zh: 吾屬今為虜矣！」

translations.literal: We are captives now!
translations.idiomatic: We are prisoners already!

sentences.zh: 後玄感將西入，福嗣竟亡歸東都。

translations.literal: Later when Xuangan was about to march west, Fusi in the end fled and returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Xuangan turned west, Fusi escaped back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時李子雄勸玄感速稱尊號，玄感以問於密。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zixiong urged Xuangan quickly to assume the exalted title; Xuangan asked Mi about it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiong urged Xuangan to declare himself emperor without delay; Xuangan consulted Mi.

sentences.zh: 密曰：「昔陳勝自欲稱王，張耳諫而被外，魏武將求九錫，荀彧止而見疎。

translations.literal: Mi said, "Formerly Chen Sheng wished to declare himself king on his own; Zhang Er remonstrated and was cast out. When the Earl of Wei of Cao was about to seek the Nine Bestowals, Xun Yu stopped him and was estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "When Chen Sheng sought a royal title, Zhang Er warned him and was cast aside. When Cao Cao moved toward the Nine Gifts, Xun Yu opposed him and was distanced.

sentences.zh: 今者密欲正言，還恐追蹤二子，阿諛順意，又非密之本圖。

translations.literal: Now if Mi wishes to speak honestly, I still fear following in the tracks of those two men; to flatter and accord with your wish is again not Mi's original intent.
translations.idiomatic: If I speak honestly, I risk sharing their fate; to flatter you goes against everything I stand for.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 兵起已來，雖復頻捷，至於郡縣，未有從者。

translations.literal: Since troops were raised, though there have again been frequent victories, as for the districts and counties there have been none who followed.
translations.idiomatic: Though we have won battle after battle, no district or county has joined us.

sentences.zh: 東都守禦尚強，天下救兵益至，公當身先士眾，早定關中。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital's defense is still strong, relief armies from across the realm increase daily; you ought to take the lead before the soldiers and settle Guanzhong early.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang still holds firm, and relief armies gather daily. You should lead the charge yourself and secure Guanzhong without delay.

sentences.zh: 廼欲急自尊崇，何示不廣也！」

translations.literal: Yet you wish hastily to exalt yourself — what narrowness does this show!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you rush to crown yourself—what message of grand vision does that send!

sentences.zh: 玄感笑而止。

translations.literal: Xuangan laughed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan only laughed and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 及宇文述、來護兒等軍且至，玄感謂密曰：「計將安出？」

translations.literal: When the armies of Yuwen Shu, Lai Huer, and the others were about to arrive, Xuangan said to Mi, "What plan will you set forth?
translations.idiomatic: As Yuwen Shu, Lai Huer, and other imperial forces drew near, Xuangan asked Mi, "What is our plan?

sentences.zh: 密曰：「元弘嗣統強兵於隴右，今可揚言其反，遣使迎公，因此入關，可得紿眾。」

translations.literal: Mi said, "Yuan Hongsi commands strong troops in Longyou; now we can spread word that he has rebelled and send envoys to welcome you; thereby entering the passes we can deceive the host."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "Yuan Hongsi holds strong forces in Longyou. Spread word that he has rebelled and summon him. March into the passes under that pretext and you can rally the troops."

sentences.zh: 玄感遂以密謀，號令其眾，因引西入。

translations.literal: Xuangan thereupon used Mi's scheme, proclaimed it to his host, and thus led them westward in.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan adopted Mi's plan, proclaimed it to his army, and marched west.

sentences.zh: 至陝縣，欲圍弘農宮，密諫之曰：「公今詐眾入西，軍事在速，況乃追兵將至，安可稽留！

translations.literal: Reaching Shaan county, he wished to besiege Hongnong Palace; Mi remonstrated, saying, "You now deceive the host to enter west — military affairs depend on speed; moreover pursuing troops are about to arrive — how can you delay!
translations.idiomatic: At Shaan county he wanted to besiege Hongnong Palace. Mi urged him: "You have tricked the army into marching west—speed is everything, and the pursuers are close. How can we linger!

sentences.zh: 若前不得據關，退無所守，大眾一散，何以自全？」

translations.literal: If ahead you cannot seize the passes, behind there is nowhere to hold, the great host scatters at once — how will you preserve yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Fail to seize the passes and with no refuge behind, the army will scatter—how then will any of us survive?

sentences.zh: 玄感不從，遂圍之，三日攻不能拔，方引而西。

translations.literal: Xuangan would not follow; he thereupon besieged it; for three days he attacked but could not take it, and only then led his forces westward.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan refused. He besieged the palace for three days without success, then marched on west.

sentences.zh: 至於閿鄉，追兵遂及。

translations.literal: Reaching Wen village, the pursuing troops then caught up.
translations.idiomatic: At Wen village the pursuers overtook him.

sentences.zh: 玄感敗，密間行入關，與玄感從叔詢相隨，匿於馮翊詢妻之舍。

translations.literal: Xuangan was defeated; Mi went by secret paths into the passes, followed together with Xuangan's cousin by marriage Xun, and hid in the home of Xun's wife in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was defeated, Mi stole into the passes with Xuangan's cousin Xun and hid in Xun's wife's house in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 尋為鄰人所告，遂捕獲，囚於京兆獄。

translations.literal: Before long he was reported by neighbors, was seized, and imprisoned in the Jingzhao jail.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors soon denounced them; Mi was seized and thrown into the Jingzhao prison.

sentences.zh: 是時煬帝在高陽，與其黨俱送帝所。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yang was at Gaoyang; together with his faction they were all sent to the emperor's location.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Gaoyang; Mi and his companions were sent to him there.

sentences.zh: 在途謂其徒曰：「吾等之命，同於朝露，若至高陽，必為葅醢。

translations.literal: On the road he said to his companions, "Our lives are like morning dew — if we reach Gaoyang we shall surely be made into minced meat.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he told his fellows, "Our lives are as morning dew. Once we reach Gaoyang we will be chopped to mince.

sentences.zh: 今道中猶可為計，安得行就鼎鑊，不規逃避也？」

translations.literal: Now on the road we can still make plans — how can we merely go to meet the cauldron and seething pot without plotting escape?
translations.idiomatic: We can still act while on the road. Why walk straight to the cauldron without planning our escape?

sentences.zh: 眾咸然之。

translations.literal: The host all agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 其徒多有金，密令出示使者曰：「吾等死日，此金並留付公，幸用相瘞。

translations.literal: Many of his companions had gold; Mi ordered it shown to the escort and said, "On the day we die this gold is all left for you, sir — we hope you will use it to bury us properly.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his companions had gold. Mi showed it to the escort and said, "On the day we die, leave this gold with you for a decent burial.

sentences.zh: 其餘即皆報德。」

translations.literal: The remainder will all repay your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: What remains is yours in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 使者利其金，遂相然許。

translations.literal: The escort was greedy for the gold and thereupon agreed among themselves to consent.
translations.idiomatic: The escorts, tempted by the gold, agreed.

sentences.zh: 及出關外，防禁漸弛，密請通巿酒食，每讌飲喧譁竟夕，使者不以為意。

translations.literal: When they left the passes the guard gradually loosened; Mi requested permission to buy wine and food in the market; each feast they drank and made noise all evening, and the escorts paid no mind.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the passes the guard slackened. Mi secured permission to buy wine and food, and each night they feasted until dawn while the escorts took no notice.

sentences.zh: 行次邯鄲，夜宿村中，密等七人皆穿牆而遁，與王仲伯亡抵平原賊帥郝孝德。

translations.literal: Traveling and stopping at Handan, they lodged at night in a village; Mi and seven others all broke through the wall and fled, and with Wang Zhongbo escaped to Plain bandit chief Hao Xiaode.
translations.idiomatic: At Handan they lodged in a village by night. Mi and seven others broke through the wall and fled with Wang Zhongbo to the bandit leader Hao Xiaode on the Plain.

sentences.zh: 孝德不甚禮之，備遭饑饉，至削樹皮而食。

translations.literal: Xiaode did not treat them with much courtesy; they further suffered famine, reaching the point of stripping tree bark to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode showed them little courtesy. They suffered famine so severe they stripped bark from trees to eat.

sentences.zh: 仲伯潛歸天水，密詣淮陽，舍於村中，變姓名稱劉智遠，聚徒教授。

translations.literal: Zhongbo secretly returned to Tianshui; Mi went to Huaiyang, lodged in a village, changed his name to Liu Zhiyuan, gathered disciples, and taught.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongbo slipped back to Tianshui. Mi made for Huaiyang, lodged in a village under the name Liu Zhiyuan, gathered students, and taught.

sentences.zh: 經數月，密鬱鬱不得志，為五言詩曰：「金風蕩初節，玉露凋晚林。

translations.literal: After several months, Mi was depressed and unfulfilled; he composed a pentasyllabic poem, saying: "The golden wind stirs the season's first turn; jade dew withers the late woods.
translations.idiomatic: After several months Li Mi remained restless and thwarted in ambition. He wrote a pentasyllabic poem: "Golden wind shakes the year's first turning; jade dew withers the late woods.

sentences.zh: 此夕窮塗士，空軫鬱陶心。

translations.literal: This night, a man at the end of the road—empty, the heart's pent-up grief turns.
translations.idiomatic: Tonight a wanderer at the road's end nurses only thwarted grief in vain.

sentences.zh: 眺聽良多感，慷慨獨霑襟。

translations.literal: Gazing and listening, much feeling arises; alone in generous emotion, tears soak the collar.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing and listening stir deep feeling; moved to passion, he alone wet his collar with tears.

sentences.zh: 霑襟何所為？

translations.literal: Why soak the collar? What is it for?
translations.idiomatic: Why do tears soak the collar?

sentences.zh: 悵然懷古意。

translations.literal: Sadly, he harbors thoughts of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Because he broods sadly on the heroes of old.

sentences.zh: 秦俗猶未平，漢道將何冀！

translations.literal: Qin's ways are not yet settled; what hope for Han's Way?
translations.idiomatic: Qin's ways are not yet put right—what hope remains for Han's mandate?

sentences.zh: 樊噲巿井徒，蕭何刀筆吏。

translations.literal: Fan Kuai was a market-stall man; Xiao He a clerk with knife and brush.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai was a butcher from the marketplace; Xiao He a clerk who kept accounts with knife and brush.

sentences.zh: 一朝時運合，萬古傳名器。

translations.literal: In one morning the times' fortune aligned; for ten thousand ages their names and vessels are transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune turned in a single morning, their fame endured for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 寄言世上雄，虛生真可愧。」

translations.literal: I send word to the heroes of the age: living in vain is truly shameful."
translations.idiomatic: I tell the mighty of this world: to live empty-handed is a true disgrace."

sentences.zh: 詩成而泣下數行。

translations.literal: When the poem was finished, several lines of tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished the poem, tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 時人有怪之者，以告太守趙他。

translations.literal: At the time some found him strange and reported it to the prefect Zhao Ta.
translations.idiomatic: Some in the district thought him odd and reported him to Prefect Zhao Ta.

sentences.zh: 縣捕之，密乃亡去，抵其妹夫雍丘令丘君明。

translations.literal: The county arrested him; Mi then fled, reaching his brother-in-law Qiu Junming, magistrate of Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The county sought to arrest him. Mi fled to his brother-in-law Qiu Junming, magistrate of Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 後君明從子懷義以告，帝令捕密，密得遁去，君明竟坐死。

translations.literal: Later Junming's nephew Huaiyi informed on him; the Emperor ordered Mi seized. Mi escaped; Junming in the end was punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Later Junming's nephew Huaiyi denounced him. The emperor ordered Mi captured. Mi got away, but Junming was executed in the end.

sentences.zh: 會東郡賊帥翟讓聚黨萬餘人，密歸之。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhai Rang, bandit chief of the Eastern Commandery, gathered a party of more than ten thousand; Mi joined him.
translations.idiomatic: About then Zhai Rang, rebel leader in the Eastern Commandery, mustered more than ten thousand men, and Mi threw in his lot with him.

sentences.zh: 其中有知密是玄感亡將，潛勸讓害之。

translations.literal: Among them were those who knew Mi was a fugitive general of Xuangan's; they secretly urged Rang to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Some in the band knew Mi had been a general under Yang Xuangan and quietly urged Rang to kill him.

sentences.zh: 密大懼，乃因王伯當以策干讓。

translations.literal: Mi was greatly afraid; he therefore had Wang Bodang present stratagems to win Rang over.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was terrified. He had Wang Bodang offer plans to win Rang over.

sentences.zh: 讓遣說諸小賊，所至輒降下，讓始敬焉，召與計事。

translations.literal: Rang sent him to persuade the lesser bandits; wherever he went they at once submitted. Rang then began to respect him and summoned him to counsel on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rang sent him to win over smaller bands; wherever he went they submitted. Rang came to respect him and called him into council.

sentences.zh: 密謂讓曰：「今兵眾既多，糧無所出，若曠日持久，則人馬困敝，大敵一臨，死亡無日。

translations.literal: Mi said to Rang: "Now the troops are many but grain has nowhere to come from. If the days drag on, men and horses will be worn out; when a great enemy arrives, the day of death will be near.
translations.idiomatic: Mi told Rang: "Your force is large but there is no grain. If this drags on, men and horses will be exhausted. When a strong enemy comes, you will not live to see another day.

sentences.zh: 未若直趣滎陽，休兵館穀，待士馬肥充，然可與人爭利。」

translations.literal: It would be better to strike straight for Xingyang, rest the troops and store grain, wait until men and horses are fat and full—then you can contend for advantage with others."
translations.idiomatic: Better march straight on Xingyang, rest the army and fill the granaries, and only when horses and men are strong fight for mastery."

sentences.zh: 讓從之，於是破金堤關，掠滎陽諸縣，城堡多下之。

translations.literal: Rang followed this; they then broke Jin Embankment Pass, raided the counties of Xingyang, and many fortresses submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Rang agreed. They stormed Jin Embankment Pass, plundered the Xingyang counties, and took many strongholds.

sentences.zh: 滎陽太守郇王慶及通守張須陁以兵討讓。

translations.literal: Xingyang Administrator Xun Wangqing and Acting Prefect Zhang Xuotuo led troops to attack Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyang Administrator Xun Wangqing and Acting Prefect Zhang Xuotuo marched against Rang with government troops.

sentences.zh: 讓數為須陁所敗，聞其來，大懼，將遠避之。

translations.literal: Rang had several times been defeated by Xuotuo; hearing he was coming, he was greatly afraid and was about to flee far away.
translations.idiomatic: Rang had lost repeatedly to Xuotuo. When he heard Xuotuo was coming, he panicked and prepared to flee.

sentences.zh: 密曰：「須陁勇而無謀，兵又驟勝，既驕且狠，可一戰而擒。

translations.literal: Mi said: "Xuotuo is brave but lacks stratagem; his troops have won in haste and are both arrogant and fierce—he can be captured in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "Xuotuo is brave but no strategist. His men have won too quickly—they are arrogant and brutal. One battle will take him.

sentences.zh: 公但列陣以待，保為公破之。」

translations.literal: Your Lordship need only array the ranks and wait; I guarantee to break him for you."
translations.idiomatic: Draw up your lines and wait. I pledge to defeat him for you."

sentences.zh: 讓不得已，勒兵將戰，密分兵千餘人於林木間設伏。

translations.literal: Rang had no choice; he marshaled the army to give battle. Mi divided more than a thousand men to set ambush among the trees.
translations.idiomatic: Rang had no choice but to fight. Mi posted more than a thousand men in ambush among the woods.

sentences.zh: 讓與戰不利，軍稍却，密發伏自後掩之，須陁眾潰。

translations.literal: Rang's battle went badly; the army gradually fell back. Mi launched the ambush from the rear to strike them; Xuotuo's host collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Rang's attack faltered and his line gave ground. Mi sprang the ambush from behind; Xuotuo's army broke.

sentences.zh: 與讓合擊，大破之，遂斬須陁於陣。

translations.literal: Together with Rang he struck in combined attack, routed them utterly, and beheaded Xuotuo on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Mi and Rang struck together, routed the enemy, and cut down Xuotuo in the fray.

sentences.zh: 讓於是令密建牙，別統所部。

translations.literal: Rang thereupon had Mi raise his own standard and command his division separately.
translations.idiomatic: Rang then let Mi set up his own headquarters and lead his own troops.

sentences.zh: 密復說讓曰：「昏主蒙塵，播蕩吳、越，蝟毛競起，海內饑荒。

translations.literal: Mi again urged Rang: "The benighted ruler is lost in dust; turmoil sweeps Wu and Yue; bandits rise thick as hedgehog quills; famine fills the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Mi urged Rang again: "The blinded emperor wanders in exile. Chaos roils Wu and Yue. Rebels sprout like hedgehog bristles. Famine grips the land.

sentences.zh: 明公以英桀之才，而統驍雄之旅，宜當廓清天下，誅剪羣凶，豈可求食草間，常為小盜而已！

translations.literal: Your Lordship, with heroic talent, commands fierce champions—you ought to clear the realm, cut down the wicked, not grub for food in the grass and remain a petty bandit forever!
translations.idiomatic: You have heroic talent and command fierce warriors. You should pacify the realm and destroy the wicked—not live as a petty thief forever, scraping a living in the weeds!

sentences.zh: 今東都士庶，中外離心，留守諸官，政令不一。

translations.literal: Now the gentry and commoners of the Eastern Capital are divided at home and abroad; the officials left to guard them do not agree in policy.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital is divided within and without. The officials left behind cannot agree on orders.

sentences.zh: 明公親率大眾，直掩興洛倉，發粟以賑窮乏，遠近孰不歸附！

translations.literal: If Your Lordship personally leads the great host straight against the Xingluo Granary, opens the grain to relieve the destitute—who near or far would not submit!
translations.idiomatic: Lead your main force straight on the Xingluo Granary, open the stores and feed the starving—who would not rally to you?

sentences.zh: 百萬之眾，一朝可集，先發制人，此機不可失也。」

translations.literal: A host of a million can be gathered in a morning; strike first and control others—this opportunity must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: A million men could gather in a day. Strike first—this chance will not come again."

sentences.zh: 讓曰：「僕起隴畝之間，望不至此。

translations.literal: Rang said: "I rose from between the furrows; I never aspired to this.
translations.idiomatic: Rang said: "I was a farmer. I never dreamed of such heights.

sentences.zh: 必如所圖，請君先發，僕領諸軍，便為後殿。

translations.literal: If it must be as you plan, please you go first; I will lead the armies and serve as the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: If we do as you say, you go first. I will follow with the rest and cover the rear.

sentences.zh: 得倉之日，當別議之。」

translations.literal: The day we take the granary, we shall discuss further."
translations.idiomatic: When the granary is ours, we can talk again."

sentences.zh: 密與讓領精兵七千人，以大業十三年春，出陽城，北踰方山，自羅口襲興洛倉，破之。

translations.literal: Mi and Rang led seven thousand picked troops. In spring of the thirteenth year of Daye they left Yangcheng, crossed north over Fang Mountain, and from Luokou raided the Xingluo Granary and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi and Rang led seven thousand elite troops. In spring of Daye year 13 they left Yangcheng, crossed Fang Mountain to the north, and stormed the Xingluo Granary through Luokou.

sentences.zh: 開倉恣民所取，老弱繈負，道路不絕。

translations.literal: They opened the granary and let the people take freely; old and young came on one another's backs, the road unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the stores to the people. Old and young came in endless streams, children on their backs, filling the roads.

sentences.zh: 越王侗武賁郎將劉長恭率步騎二萬五千討密，密一戰破之，長恭僅以身免。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong's Brave Attendant General Liu Changgong led twenty-five thousand foot and horse to attack Mi; Mi broke them in one battle, and Changgong barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changgong, Brave Attendant General to Prince of Yue Yang Tong, marched on Mi with twenty-five thousand men. Mi routed him in one fight; Changgong barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 讓於是推密為主。

translations.literal: Rang thereupon urged Mi to be lord.
translations.idiomatic: Rang then pressed Mi to become leader.

sentences.zh: 密城洛口周廻四十里以居之。

translations.literal: Mi fortified Luokou, forty li in circuit, and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fortified Luokou—a circuit of forty li—and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 房彥藻說下豫州，東都大懼。

translations.literal: Fang Yanzao persuaded and took Yuzhou; the Eastern Capital was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanzao won over Yuzhou. The Eastern Capital was terrified.

sentences.zh: 讓上密號為魏公。

translations.literal: Rang submitted to Mi the title Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Rang offered Mi the title Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 密初辭不受，諸將等固請，乃從之。

translations.literal: At first Mi declined and would not accept; the generals firmly pressed him, and he then assented.
translations.idiomatic: Mi refused at first, but when the generals insisted he accepted.

sentences.zh: 設壇場，即位，稱元年，置官屬以房彥藻為左長史，邴元真右長史，楊德方左司馬，鄭德韜右司馬。

translations.literal: He set up an altar, took the throne, proclaimed the first year of his reign, and appointed officials: Fang Yanzao Left Chief Clerk, Bing Yuanzhen Right Chief Clerk, Yang Defang Left Marshal, Zheng Detao Right Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He raised an altar, took the throne, proclaimed year one, and appointed a court: Fang Yanzao as Left Chief Clerk, Bing Yuanzhen as Right Chief Clerk, Yang Defang as Left Marshal, Zheng Detao as Right Marshal.

sentences.zh: 拜讓司徒，封東郡公。

translations.literal: He invested Rang as Minister of Works and enfeoffed him as Duke of the Eastern Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He made Rang Minister of Works and Duke of the Eastern Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其將帥封拜各有差。

translations.literal: His generals received investiture and appointment each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders received titles and ranks in due order.

sentences.zh: 長白山賊孟讓掠東都，燒豐都市而歸。

translations.literal: The Changbai Mountain bandit Meng Rang raided the Eastern Capital, burned Fengdu Market, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Rang of Changbai Mountain raided the Eastern Capital, burned Fengdu Market, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 密攻下鞏縣，獲縣長柴孝和，拜為護軍。

translations.literal: Mi attacked and took Gong County, captured the magistrate Chai Xiaohe, and appointed him Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Mi took Gong County, captured Magistrate Chai Xiaohe, and made him Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 武賁郎將裴仁基以武牢歸密，因遣仁基與孟讓率兵二萬餘人襲迴洛倉，破之，燒天津橋，遂縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: Brave Attendant General Pei Renji surrendered Wulao to Mi. Mi then sent Renji and Meng Rang with more than twenty thousand men to raid Huiluo Granary, took it, burned Tianjin Bridge, and then let the troops plunder freely.
translations.idiomatic: Brave Attendant General Pei Renji surrendered Wulao to Mi. Mi sent Renji and Meng Rang with over twenty thousand men against Huiluo Granary. They took it, burned Tianjin Bridge, and sacked the city.

sentences.zh: 東都出兵乘之，仁基等大敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital sent troops to strike while their advantage held; Renji and the rest were utterly defeated and barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital counterattacked. Renji and the others were crushed; only a few got away alive.

sentences.zh: 密復親率兵三萬逼東都，將軍段達、武賁郎將高毗、劉長恭等出兵七萬拒之，戰於故都，官軍敗走，密復下廻洛倉而據之。

translations.literal: Mi again personally led thirty thousand troops to press the Eastern Capital. General Duan Da, Brave Attendant Generals Gao Pi and Liu Changgong, and others led seventy thousand to resist. They fought at the old capital; the government army was routed and fled. Mi again took Huiluo Granary and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi led thirty thousand men against the Eastern Capital himself. General Duan Da, Brave Attendant Generals Gao Pi and Liu Changgong, and others met him with seventy thousand. At the old capital the government forces broke and fled. Mi reoccupied Huiluo Granary.

sentences.zh: 俄而德韜、德方俱死，復以鄭頲為左司馬，鄭虔象為右司馬。

translations.literal: Before long Detao and Defang both died; he again appointed Zheng Ting Left Marshal and Zheng Qianxiang Right Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Detao and Defang died. Mi replaced them with Zheng Ting as Left Marshal and Zheng Qianxiang as Right Marshal.

sentences.zh: 柴孝和說密曰：「秦地阻山帶河，西楚背之而亡，漢高都之而霸。

translations.literal: Chai Xiaohe urged Mi: "Qin's land is blocked by mountains and girdled by rivers. Western Chu turned its back on it and perished; Han Gaozu made it his capital and became hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Xiaohe advised Mi: "The Qin heartland is walled by mountains and rivers. Western Chu held it with its back to the land and fell. Gaozu made it his capital and ruled the realm.

sentences.zh: 如愚意者，令仁基守廻洛，翟讓守洛口，明公親簡精銳，西襲長安，百姓孰不郊迎，必當有征無戰。

translations.literal: In my humble view, let Renji hold Huiluo, Zhai Rang hold Luokou; Your Lordship personally choose picked troops, strike west at Chang'an—the common people, who would not welcome you at the suburbs? Surely there would be campaigns without battles.
translations.idiomatic: My counsel: leave Renji at Huiluo and Zhai Rang at Luokou. Take your best troops west against Chang'an. The people will greet you on the roads. You can win the capital without a fight.

sentences.zh: 既剋京邑，業固兵強，方更長驅崤、函，掃蕩京、洛，傳檄指撝，天下可定。

translations.literal: Once the capital is taken, your enterprise will be firm and your troops strong; then you can drive at length through Xiao and Han, sweep Jing and Luo, issue proclamations and command—and the realm can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once you hold the western capital your position will be secure. Then drive through the passes, sweep the eastern capitals, issue edicts—and the realm is yours.

sentences.zh: 但今英雄競起，實恐他人我先，一朝失之，噬臍何及！」

translations.literal: But now heroes rise in rivalry; I truly fear another will get there before us. Lose it in a morning—how can gnawing the navel help!"
translations.idiomatic: But rivals are rising everywhere. Another may reach Chang'an first. Miss this chance and you will regret it forever."

sentences.zh: 密曰：「君之所圖，僕亦思之久矣，誠為上策。

translations.literal: Mi said: "What you propose—I have pondered it long; it is truly the superior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "I have weighed that plan for a long time. It is the best course.

sentences.zh: 但昏主尚在，從兵猶眾，我之所部，並山東人，既見未下洛陽，何肯相隨西入！

translations.literal: But the benighted ruler is still alive, his following troops are still many, and those under my command are all men of the eastern mountains. Seeing that Luoyang is not yet taken, how would they agree to follow west!
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor still lives, his armies are large, and my men are all from the east. They have not seen Luoyang fall—why would they march west with me?

sentences.zh: 諸將出於羣盜，留之各競雌雄。

translations.literal: The generals came out of the bandit hosts; leave them behind and each will contend for supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: My commanders were bandits themselves. Leave them behind and they will fight each other for power.

sentences.zh: 若然者，殆將敗矣。」

translations.literal: If it were so, we would nearly be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: That way lies ruin."

sentences.zh: 孝和曰：「誠如公言，非所及也。

translations.literal: Xiaohe said: "Truly as you say—I cannot match it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe said: "You are right. I cannot argue.

sentences.zh: 大軍既未可西出，請間行觀隙。」

translations.literal: Since the great army cannot yet go west, I ask to go by hidden routes and watch for openings."
translations.idiomatic: If the main force cannot go west yet, let me scout by side routes and watch for a chance."

sentences.zh: 密從之。

translations.literal: Mi assented.
translations.idiomatic: Mi agreed.

sentences.zh: 孝和與數十騎至陝縣，山賊歸之者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Xiaohe with several dozen horsemen reached Shan County; mountain bandits who submitted to him numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe rode to Shan County with a few dozen men. More than ten thousand mountain rebels joined him.

sentences.zh: 密時兵鋒甚銳，每入苑，與官軍連戰。

translations.literal: At the time Mi's military edge was very sharp; each time he entered the park he fought continuously with the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's army was at its peak. Each raid into the imperial park brought repeated clashes with government troops.

sentences.zh: 會密為流矢所中，臥於營內，後數日，東都出兵擊之。

translations.literal: It happened that Mi was struck by a stray arrow; he lay within the camp. Several days later the Eastern Capital sent troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was hit by a stray arrow and lay in camp. Days later the Eastern Capital attacked.

sentences.zh: 密眾大潰，棄廻洛倉，歸洛口。

translations.literal: Mi's host collapsed utterly; they abandoned Huiluo Granary and returned to Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's army broke. They abandoned Huiluo Granary and fell back to Luokou.

sentences.zh: 孝和之眾聞密退，各分散而去。

translations.literal: When Xiaohe's troops heard Mi had retreated, each scattered and went away.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe's men heard of the retreat and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 孝和輕騎歸密。

translations.literal: Xiaohe with light horse returned to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe rode back to Mi with a small escort.

sentences.zh: 帝遣王世充率江、淮勁卒五萬來討密，密逆拒之，戰不利。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Wang Shichong with fifty thousand crack troops from the Jiang and Huai to attack Mi; Mi met them in resistance but the battle went badly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Shichong with fifty thousand Jiang-Huai veterans against Mi. Mi met him but lost the fight.

sentences.zh: 柴孝和溺死於洛水，密甚傷之。

translations.literal: Chai Xiaohe drowned in the Luo River; Mi grieved for him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Xiaohe drowned in the Luo. Mi mourned him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 世充營於洛西，與密相拒百餘日。

translations.literal: Shichong camped west of the Luo and faced Mi in stalemate for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong camped west of the Luo and faced Mi for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 武陽郡丞元寶藏、黎陽賊帥李文相、洹水賊帥張昇、清河賊帥趙君德、平原賊帥郝孝德並歸於密，共襲破黎陽倉據之。

translations.literal: Wuyang Assistant Prefect Yuan Baocang, Liyang bandit chief Li Wenxiang, Huanshui bandit chief Zhang Sheng, Qinghe bandit chief Zhao Junde, and Plain bandit chief Hao Xiaode all submitted to Mi. Together they raided and took Liyang Granary and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Baocang of Wuyang, Li Wenxiang of Liyang, Zhang Sheng of Huanshui, Zhao Junde of Qinghe, and Hao Xiaode of the Plain all joined Mi. Together they stormed and held Liyang Granary.

sentences.zh: 周法明舉江、黃之地以附密，齊郡賊帥徐圓朗、任城大俠徐師仁、淮陽太守趙他等前後款附，以千百數。

translations.literal: Zhou Faming raised the lands of the Jiang and Huang for Mi; Qi Commandery bandit chief Xu Yuanlang, Rencheng champion Xu Shiren, Huaiyang Prefect Zhao Ta, and others before and after came in submission—by the hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Faming brought the Jiang and Huang regions to Mi. Xu Yuanlang of Qi, the champion Xu Shiren of Rencheng, Huaiyang Prefect Zhao Ta, and many others submitted—in thousands.

sentences.zh: 翟讓所部王儒信勸讓為大冢宰，總統眾務，以奪密權。

translations.literal: Wang Ruxin of Zhai Rang's division urged Rang to become Grand Chancellor and oversee all affairs, to seize Mi's power.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruxin, a follower of Zhai Rang, urged Rang to become Grand Chancellor and run everything, stripping power from Mi.

sentences.zh: 讓兄寬復謂讓曰：「天子止可自作，安得與人？

translations.literal: Rang's elder brother Kuan again said to Rang: "The Son of Heaven can only be made by oneself—how can one share it with another?
translations.idiomatic: Rang's brother Kuan told him: "An emperor makes himself—how can you share the throne with anyone?

sentences.zh: 汝若不能作，我當為之。」

translations.literal: If you cannot do it, I will do it for you."
translations.idiomatic: If you will not take it, I will."

sentences.zh: 密聞其言，有圖讓之計。

translations.literal: When Mi heard these words, he formed a plan to dispose of Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Mi overheard and plotted to kill Rang.

sentences.zh: 會世充列陣而至，讓出拒之，為世充所擊退者數百步。

translations.literal: It happened that Shichong drew up his ranks and came; Rang went out to resist and was driven back several hundred paces by Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong advanced in battle order. Rang went out to meet him and was driven back hundreds of paces.

sentences.zh: 密與單雄信等率精銳赴之，世充敗走。

translations.literal: Mi with Shan Xiongxin and others led picked troops to the rescue; Shichong was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Mi rushed up with Shan Xiongxin and picked troops. Shichong broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 讓欲乘勝進破其營，會日暮，密固止之。

translations.literal: Rang wished to press the victory and break Shichong's camp, but night fell and Mi firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Rang wanted to pursue and smash Shichong's camp, but night fell and Mi held him back.

sentences.zh: 明日，讓與數百人至密所，欲為宴樂。

translations.literal: The next day Rang came with several hundred men to Mi's quarters, intending feasting and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Rang came to Mi's camp with several hundred men for a feast.

sentences.zh: 密具饌以待之，其所將左右，各分令就食。

translations.literal: Mi prepared a banquet to await him; those Rang brought on left and right were each separately told to go eat.
translations.idiomatic: Mi set a banquet and sent Rang's followers to eat in separate groups.

sentences.zh: 諸門並設備，讓不之覺也。

translations.literal: At every gate preparations were set; Rang did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Armed men waited at every gate. Rang noticed nothing.

sentences.zh: 密引讓入坐，有好弓，出示讓，遂令讓射。

translations.literal: Mi led Rang in to sit; there was a fine bow—he showed it to Rang and then had Rang shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Mi seated Rang and showed him a fine bow, then asked him to draw it.

sentences.zh: 讓引滿將發，密遣壯士蔡建自後斬之，殞於牀下。

translations.literal: Rang drew the bow full and was about to release; Mi sent the stalwart Cai Jian to cut him down from behind, and he perished beneath the couch.
translations.idiomatic: As Rang drew the bow, Mi had Cai Jian strike him from behind. He died on the couch.

sentences.zh: 遂殺其兄寬及王儒信，并其從者亦有死焉。

translations.literal: He then killed Rang's brother Kuan and Wang Ruxin; among their followers some also died.
translations.idiomatic: Mi killed Kuan and Wang Ruxin too. Some of their attendants died in the tumult.

sentences.zh: 讓所部將徐世勣，為亂兵所斫中，重創，密遽止之，僅而得免。

translations.literal: Rang's division general Xu Shiji was hacked by the disorderly troops and badly wounded; Mi hurriedly stopped them, and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiji, a general under Rang, was cut in the confusion and badly wounded. Mi stopped the slaughter just in time to save him.

sentences.zh: 單雄信等皆叩頭求哀，密並釋而慰諭之。

translations.literal: Shan Xiongxin and the rest all knocked their heads begging for mercy; Mi all released them and comforted them with words.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin and the others kowtowed for mercy. Mi pardoned them and spoke reassuringly.

sentences.zh: 於是率左右數百人詣讓本營。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led several hundred of his close attendants to Rang's original camp.
translations.idiomatic: Then Mi went with several hundred guards to Rang's old camp.

sentences.zh: 王伯當、邴元真、單雄信等入營，告以殺讓之意，眾無敢動者。

translations.literal: Wang Bodang, Bing Yuanzhen, Shan Xiongxin, and others entered the camp and announced the intent to kill Rang; none in the host dared move.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bodang, Bing Yuanzhen, and Shan Xiongxin entered and announced Rang's death. No one dared stir.

sentences.zh: 乃令徐世勣、單雄信、王伯當分統其眾。

translations.literal: He then ordered Xu Shiji, Shan Xiongxin, and Wang Bodang each to command Rang's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mi put Xu Shiji, Shan Xiongxin, and Wang Bodang in command of Rang's men.

sentences.zh: 未幾，世充夜襲倉城，密逆拒破之，斬武賁郎將費青奴。

translations.literal: Before long Shichong raided the granary city by night; Mi met and repelled him, beheading Brave Attendant General Fei Qingnu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shichong raided the granary by night. Mi drove him off and killed Brave Attendant General Fei Qingnu.

sentences.zh: 世充復移營洛北，南對鞏縣，其後遂於洛水造浮橋，悉眾以擊密。

translations.literal: Shichong again moved camp north of the Luo, facing Gong County to the south; afterward he built a pontoon bridge on the Luo and led his entire force against Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong moved north of the Luo opposite Gong County, then built a pontoon bridge and brought his whole army against Mi.

sentences.zh: 密與千騎拒之，不利而退。

translations.literal: Mi with a thousand horse met him in resistance; the battle went badly and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mi met him with a thousand cavalry, lost, and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 世充因薄其城下，密簡銳卒數百人，分為三隊出擊之。

translations.literal: Shichong therefore pressed close beneath the walls; Mi chose several hundred sharp troops, divided them into three teams, and sallied to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong pressed the walls. Mi picked several hundred elite men in three columns and sallied out.

sentences.zh: 官軍稍却，自相陷溺，死者數萬人，武賁郎將楊威、王辯、霍世舉、劉長恭、梁德重、董智通等諸將率皆沒于陣。

translations.literal: The government army gradually fell back, drowning one another; dead numbered in the tens of thousands. Brave Attendant Generals Yang Wei, Wang Bian, Huo Shiju, Liu Changgong, Liang Dezhong, Dong Zhitong, and other commanders all perished on the field.
translations.idiomatic: The government line gave way. Men trampled one another into the river; tens of thousands died. Generals Yang Wei, Wang Bian, Huo Shiju, Liu Changgong, Liang Dezhong, Dong Zhitong, and many others fell in the battle.

sentences.zh: 世充僅而獲免，不敢還東都，遂走河陽。

translations.literal: Shichong barely escaped; he dared not return to the Eastern Capital and fled to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong barely got away. He dared not return to the Eastern Capital and fled to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 其夜雨雪尺餘，眾隨之者，死亡殆盡。

translations.literal: That night snow and rain fell more than a foot deep; of the host that followed him, nearly all died.
translations.idiomatic: That night more than a foot of snow fell. Nearly all who followed him perished in the cold.

sentences.zh: 密於是修金墉故城居之，眾三十餘萬。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon repaired the old city of Jinyong and dwelt there; his host numbered more than three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fortified the old city of Jinyong and made it his seat. His force exceeded three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 復來攻上春門，留守韋津出拒戰，密擊敗之，執津於陣。

translations.literal: He again came to attack Shangchun Gate; the left-behind defender Wei Jin went out to resist in battle. Mi defeated him and seized Jin on the field.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Shangchun Gate again. The garrison commander Wei Jin marched out to fight; Mi routed him and took Jin prisoner in battle.

sentences.zh: 其黨勸密即尊號，密不許。

translations.literal: His faction urged Mi to take the imperial title at once; Mi would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: His followers urged him to declare himself emperor. Mi refused.

sentences.zh: 及義師圍東都，密出軍爭之，交綏而退。

translations.literal: When the righteous army besieged the Eastern Capital, Mi led troops to contend for it; they crossed blades and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel armies besieged the Eastern Capital, Mi marched out to contest it, skirmished, and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 俄而宇文化及殺逆，率眾自江都北指黎陽，兵十餘萬。

translations.literal: Before long Yuwen Huaji committed regicide and led his host from Jiangdu north toward Liyang—more than a hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor and marched north from Jiangdu toward Liyang with more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 密乃自率步騎二萬拒之。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon personally led twenty thousand foot and horse to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to meet him.

sentences.zh: 會越王侗稱尊號，遣使者授密太尉、尚書令、東南道大行臺、行軍元帥、魏國公，令先平化及，然後入朝輔政。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince of Yue Tong assumed the imperial title and sent envoys to invest Mi as Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit, Campaign Marshal, and Duke of Wei, ordering him first to pacify Huaji and then enter court to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Yang Tong took the throne and sent envoys making Mi Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Commissioner for the Southeast, Campaign Marshal, and Duke of Wei, with orders to defeat Huaji first and then enter court as regent.

sentences.zh: 密遣使報謝焉。

translations.literal: Mi sent envoys to return thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Mi sent envoys to thank him.

sentences.zh: 化及與密相遇，密知其軍少食，利在急戰，故不與交鋒，又遏其歸路，使不得西。

translations.literal: Huaji and Mi met. Mi knew his army was short of grain and that the advantage lay in swift battle, so he would not cross blades; he also blocked his route of return so he could not go west.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji and Mi met, Mi knew Huaji's men were short of food and would want a quick fight. Mi refused battle and blocked the road west so Huaji could not retreat.

sentences.zh: 密遣徐世勣守倉城，化及攻之，不能下。

translations.literal: Mi sent Xu Shiji to hold the granary city; Huaji attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi left Xu Shiji to hold the granary city. Huaji attacked but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 密與化及隔水而語，密數之曰：「卿本匈奴皁隸破野頭耳，父兄子弟並受隋室厚恩，富貴累世，至妻公主，光榮隆顯，舉朝莫二。

translations.literal: Mi and Huaji spoke across the water. Mi reproached him: "You were originally a black-slave bondsman of the Xiongnu, Poyetou—father, brothers, sons, and nephews all received thick favor from the Sui house, wealth and honor for generations, even marrying an imperial princess, glory lofty and manifest, unmatched in court.
translations.idiomatic: Mi and Huaji shouted across the river. Mi denounced him: "You were a Xiongnu bondsman from Poyetou. Your whole clan enjoyed Sui favor for generations—even an imperial princess as wife. No one in court outshone you.

sentences.zh: 荷國士之遇者，當須國士報之，豈容主上失德，不能死諫，反因眾叛，躬行殺虐，誅及子孫，傍立支庶，擅自尊崇，欲規篡奪，污辱妃后，枉害無辜？

translations.literal: One who receives a champion's treatment should repay like a champion—how can you, when the ruler loses virtue, fail to die in remonstrance, yet instead follow the multitude in rebellion, personally carry out slaughter, execute sons and grandsons, set up a collateral line beside you, arrogate supreme honor, scheme usurpation, defile consorts and queens, and wrongly harm the innocent?
translations.idiomatic: A man treated as a champion should die for his lord. When the emperor lost his way you should have remonstrated unto death—not rebel, butcher the imperial house, set up a puppet, seize the throne, and ravage the innocent.

sentences.zh: 不追諸葛瞻之忠誠，乃為霍禹之惡逆。

translations.literal: You do not pursue Zhuge Zhan's loyalty and devotion, yet act as Huo Yu's wicked rebel.
translations.idiomatic: You lack Zhuge Zhan's loyalty and imitate Huo Yu's treason.

sentences.zh: 天地所不容，人神所莫祐，擁逼良善，將欲何之！

translations.literal: Heaven and earth will not contain you; men and spirits will not bless you. You drive good people—where do you think you are going!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth reject you. Gods and men forsake you. Where can you drive honest men!

sentences.zh: 今若速來歸我，尚可得全後嗣。」

translations.literal: If you come quickly and submit to me, you may yet preserve your descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Submit to me now and your line may yet survive."

sentences.zh: 化及默然，俯視良久，乃瞋目大言曰：「共你論相殺事，何須作書語邪？」

translations.literal: Huaji was silent, looked down a long while, then glared and said in a great voice: "We are talking about killing each other—why need you make book-speech?"
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was silent, then glared and roared: "This is a fight to the death—why lecture me like a book!"

sentences.zh: 密謂從者曰：「化及庸懦如此，忽欲圖為帝王，斯乃趙高、聖公之流，吾當折杖驅之耳。」

translations.literal: Mi told his followers: "Huaji is so mediocre and cowardly, yet suddenly wants to be Son of Heaven—he is of the sort of Zhao Gao and the Duke of Sheng. I need only break a staff and drive him off."
translations.idiomatic: Mi told his men: "Huaji is this feeble, yet dreams of empire—like Zhao Gao or the Duke of Sheng. I will break a stick and drive him off."

sentences.zh: 化及盛修攻具，以逼黎陽倉城，密領輕騎五百馳赴之。

translations.literal: Huaji greatly repaired siege engines to press the Liyang granary city; Mi led five hundred light horse in a rush thither.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji built siege engines against Liyang granary. Mi galloped there with five hundred light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 倉城兵又出相應，焚其攻具，經夜火不滅。

translations.literal: The granary city troops also sallied in response, burned his siege engines, and through the night the fire did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from the granary sallied out, burned the siege engines, and the blaze burned all night.

sentences.zh: 密知化及糧且盡，因偽與和，以敝其眾。

translations.literal: Mi knew Huaji's grain was nearly exhausted; he therefore feigned peace with him to wear out his host.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Huaji's food was almost gone, Mi feigned peace to wear down his army.

sentences.zh: 化及不之悟，大喜，恣其兵食，冀密饋之。

translations.literal: Huaji did not perceive it and was greatly pleased; he let his troops eat freely, hoping Mi would supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji fell for it and let his men eat freely, expecting Mi to feed them.

sentences.zh: 會密下有人獲罪，亡投化及，具言密情。

translations.literal: It happened that someone under Mi who had committed a crime fled to Huaji and fully explained Mi's intent.
translations.idiomatic: A man under Mi who had committed a crime fled to Huaji and revealed the whole plan.

sentences.zh: 化及大怒，其食又盡，乃渡永濟渠，與密戰于童山之下，自辰達酉。

translations.literal: Huaji was greatly enraged; his food was again exhausted. He then crossed the Yongji Canal and fought Mi below Tong Mountain from the hour chen until the hour you.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji flew into a rage. When his food ran out he crossed the Yongji Canal and fought Mi at Tong Mountain from morning until evening.

sentences.zh: 密為流矢所中，頓於汲縣。

translations.literal: Mi was struck by a stray arrow and halted at Ji County.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was hit by a stray arrow and halted at Ji County.

sentences.zh: 化及掠汲郡，北趣魏縣，其將陳智略、張童仁等所部兵歸于密者，前後相繼。

translations.literal: Huaji plundered Ji commandery and headed north toward Wei County. His generals Chen Zhilue, Zhang Tongren, and others whose troops had submitted to Mi did so in succession before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji sacked Ji commandery and marched north toward Wei County. Generals Chen Zhilue and Zhang Tongren and others defected to Mi in droves.

sentences.zh: 初，化及以輜重留於東郡，遣其所署刑部尚書王軌守之。

translations.literal: Earlier Huaji had left baggage trains at the Eastern Commandery and sent his appointed Minister of Punishments Wang Gui to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji had left his supply train in the Eastern Commandery under his Minister of Punishments Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 至是，軌舉郡降密，以軌為滑州總管。

translations.literal: At this time Gui surrendered the whole commandery to Mi; Mi made Gui overall commander of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then surrendered the whole commandery to Mi, who made him overall commander of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 密引兵而西，遣記室參軍李儉朝於東都，執殺煬帝人于弘達以獻越王侗。

translations.literal: Mi led his army west and sent Recorder-Adjutant Li Jian to court at the Eastern Capital, seizing Yu Hongda, who had killed Emperor Yang, to present to Prince of Yue Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Mi marched west and sent Li Jian to the Eastern Capital with Yu Hongda, who had killed Emperor Yang, as a gift to Prince of Yue Yang Tong.

sentences.zh: 侗以儉為司農少卿，使之反命，召密入朝。

translations.literal: Tong made Jian Vice Minister of Agriculture and sent him back with orders summoning Mi to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong made Jian Vice Minister of Agriculture and sent him back to summon Mi to court.

sentences.zh: 密至溫縣，聞世充已殺元文都、盧楚等，乃歸金墉。

translations.literal: When Mi reached Wen County he heard Shichong had killed Yuan Wenshu, Lu Chu, and others, and returned to Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: At Wen County Mi learned Shichong had killed Yuan Wenshu and Lu Chu. He turned back to Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 世充既得擅權，乃厚賜將士，繕治器械，人心漸銳。

translations.literal: Once Shichong had seized sole power, he richly rewarded officers and soldiers and repaired weapons; morale gradually sharpened.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong seized power, lavished rewards on the troops, and rearmed them. Their spirit rose.

sentences.zh: 然密兵少衣，世充乏食，乃請交易。

translations.literal: Yet Mi's troops lacked clothing while Shichong lacked grain; they therefore requested trade.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's men lacked clothes; Shichong lacked food. They proposed to trade.

sentences.zh: 密初難之，邴元真等各求私利，遞來勸密，密遂許焉。

translations.literal: At first Mi found it difficult; Bing Yuanzhen and the rest each sought private profit and came in turn to urge Mi, and Mi then assented.
translations.idiomatic: Mi hesitated, but Bing Yuanzhen and others, seeking private gain, pressed him until he agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，東都絕糧，人歸密者，日有數百。

translations.literal: Earlier the Eastern Capital had no grain; people who submitted to Mi came by the hundreds each day.
translations.idiomatic: While the Eastern Capital starved, hundreds a day had defected to Mi.

sentences.zh: 至此，得食，而降人益少，密方悔而止。

translations.literal: Now they obtained food, and those who surrendered grew fewer. Mi then regretted it and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once they could eat elsewhere, fewer came over. Mi regretted the trade and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 密雖據倉，無府庫，兵數戰不獲賞，又厚撫初附之兵，於是眾心漸怨。

translations.literal: Though Mi held the granary, he had no treasury; the troops fought repeatedly without receiving rewards, and he also treated newly submitted troops generously—therefore hearts gradually turned resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Mi held the granary but had no treasury. His men fought without pay while new recruits were pampered. Resentment spread.

sentences.zh: 時遣邴元真守興洛倉。

translations.literal: At the time he sent Bing Yuanzhen to guard the Xingluo Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bing Yuanzhen to guard the Xingluo Granary.

sentences.zh: 元真起自微賤，性又貪鄙，宇文溫疾之，每謂密曰：「不殺元真，公難未已。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhen rose from the lowest station; his nature was also greedy and base. Yuwen Wen often hated him and would tell Mi, "If you do not kill Yuanzhen, your troubles will not end."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen came from nothing and was greedy. Yuwen Wen often told Mi, "Kill Yuanzhen or your troubles will never end."

sentences.zh: 密不答，而元真知之，陰謀叛密。

translations.literal: Mi did not answer, but Yuanzhen learned of it and secretly plotted to rebel against Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said nothing. Yuanzhen heard and plotted to betray him.

sentences.zh: 揚慶聞而告密，密固疑焉。

translations.literal: Yang Qing heard and told Mi; Mi therefore grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing warned Mi, and Mi grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 會世充悉眾來決戰，密留王伯當守金墉，自引精兵就偃師，北阻邙山以待之。

translations.literal: It happened that Shichong led his entire host to fight a decisive battle. Mi left Wang Bodang to guard Jinyong and personally led picked troops to Yanshi, blocking north by Mount Mang to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong marched out for a decisive battle. Mi left Wang Bodang at Jinyong and took elite troops to Yanshi, blocking the north at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 世充軍至，令數百騎渡御河，密遣裴行儼率眾逆之。

translations.literal: When Shichong's army arrived, he ordered several hundred horse to cross the Imperial River; Mi sent Pei Xingyan to lead the host to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent hundreds of cavalry across the Imperial River. Mi sent Pei Xingyan to meet them.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，暫交而退，行儼、孫長樂、程䶧金等驍將十數人皆遇重創，密甚惡之。

translations.literal: Night fell; they briefly crossed blades and withdrew. Xingyan, Sun Changle, Cheng Yanjin, and more than ten fierce generals all suffered grave wounds; Mi was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk they skirmished and broke off. Pei Xingyan, Sun Changle, Cheng Yanjin, and a dozen other champions were badly wounded. Mi was furious.

sentences.zh: 世充夜潛濟師，詰朝而陣，密方覺之，狼狽出戰，於是敗績，與萬餘人馳向洛口。

translations.literal: Shichong by night secretly ferried his army across; at dawn he formed ranks. Mi had just noticed and came out in disarray to fight; he was utterly defeated and with more than ten thousand men galloped toward Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong crossed the river by night and formed battle lines at dawn. Mi barely noticed in time, fought in disorder, was routed, and fled toward Luokou with ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 世充夜圍偃師，守將鄭頲為其部下所翻，以城降世充。

translations.literal: Shichong by night besieged Yanshi; the defending general Zheng Ting was turned by his subordinates, and they surrendered the city to Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong besieged Yanshi that night. His subordinates turned on defender Zheng Ting and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 密將入洛口倉城，元真已遣人潛引世充矣。

translations.literal: Mi was about to enter Luokou granary city when Yuanzhen had already secretly brought Shichong in.
translations.idiomatic: Mi tried to enter Luokou granary, but Yuanzhen had already let Shichong in.

sentences.zh: 密陰知之而不發其事，因與眾謀，待世充之兵半濟洛水，然後擊之。

translations.literal: Mi secretly knew but did not reveal the matter; he consulted with the host to wait until half Shichong's troops had crossed the Luo, then strike.
translations.idiomatic: Mi knew but said nothing. He planned to attack when half Shichong's army was still crossing the Luo.

sentences.zh: 及世充軍至，密候騎不時覺，比將出戰，世充軍悉已濟矣。

translations.literal: When Shichong's army arrived, Mi's scouts did not notice in time; by the time he was about to give battle, Shichong's army had all crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts failed to warn him in time. By the time Mi moved to fight, Shichong's whole army had crossed.

sentences.zh: 密自度不能支，引騎而遁。

translations.literal: Mi judged he could not hold; he led horse and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not hold, Mi fled with his cavalry.

sentences.zh: 元真竟以城降於世充。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen in the end surrendered the city to Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen surrendered the city to Shichong.

sentences.zh: 密眾漸離，將如黎陽。

translations.literal: Mi's host gradually scattered; he was about to go to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's army melted away. He prepared to go to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 人或謂密曰：「殺翟讓之際，徐世勣幾至於死。

translations.literal: Someone said to Mi: "When you killed Zhai Rang, Xu Shiji nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Mi: "When you killed Zhai Rang, Xu Shiji nearly died.

sentences.zh: 今創猶未復，其心安可保乎？」

translations.literal: Now his wound is not yet healed—how can his heart be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: His wounds are not healed. Can you trust him?"

sentences.zh: 密乃止。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Mi turned back.

sentences.zh: 時王伯當棄金墉，保河陽，密以輕騎自武牢渡河以歸之，謂伯當曰：「兵敗矣！

translations.literal: At the time Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong and held Heyang. Mi with light horse crossed from Wulao to join him and said to Bodang: "The army is defeated!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong for Heyang. Mi crossed from Wulao with a small escort and told Bodang, "All is lost!

sentences.zh: 久苦諸君，我今自刎，請以謝眾。」

translations.literal: Long I have wearied you all; today I will cut my own throat to apologize to the host."
translations.idiomatic: I have failed you too long. I will kill myself to answer the army."

sentences.zh: 眾皆泣，莫能仰視。

translations.literal: The host all wept; none could look up.
translations.idiomatic: All wept and could not raise their eyes.

sentences.zh: 密復曰：「諸君幸不相棄，當共歸關中。

translations.literal: Mi again said: "If you are kind enough not to abandon me, let us together return to the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "If you will not abandon me, let us go west to the Passes together.

sentences.zh: 密身雖愧無功，諸君必保富貴。」

translations.literal: Though I am ashamed at having no achievement, you all will surely preserve wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: I have achieved nothing, but you will still win wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 其府掾柳爕對曰：「昔盆子歸漢，尚食均輸，明公與長安宗族有疇昔之遇，雖不陪起義，然而阻東都，斷隋歸路，使唐國不戰而據京師，此亦公之功也。」

translations.literal: His staff officer Liu Can replied: "In old times Chizi returned to Han and still received equal provisioning from the transport office. Your Lordship and the clans of Chang'an have old acquaintance; though you did not join in raising the righteous army, yet you blocked the Eastern Capital and cut off the Sui return route, so the Tang state took the capital without battle—this too is your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Liu Can said: "When Chizi submitted to Han he was still fed from the transport offices. You have old ties in Chang'an. You did not join the uprising, but you held the Eastern Capital and cut Sui's retreat so Tang took the capital without a fight—that is your merit too."

sentences.zh: 眾咸曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The host all said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: All agreed."

sentences.zh: 密遂歸大唐，封邢國公，拜光祿卿。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon submitted to Great Tang, was enfeoffed Duke of Xing, and appointed Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Mi submitted to Tang, was made Duke of Xing, and appointed Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 裴仁基河東裴仁基，字德本。

translations.literal: Pei Renji of Hedong—Pei Renji, styled Deben.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Renji of Hedong—Pei Renji, courtesy name Deben.

sentences.zh: 祖伯鳳，周汾州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bofeng was Inspector of Fenzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bofeng had been Inspector of Fenzhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父定，上儀同。

translations.literal: His father Ding held the post of Senior Master of Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding held the rank of Senior Master of Equipage.

sentences.zh: 仁基少驍武，便弓馬。

translations.literal: In youth Renji was fierce in martial arts and skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Renji was a fierce fighter and expert archer and horseman.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，為親衞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he became an imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he joined the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，先登陷陣，拜儀同，賜物千段。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he was first to scale the walls and break the ranks; he was appointed Master of Equipage and granted a thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Chen he was first over the wall. He was made Master of Equipage and rewarded with a thousand rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 以本官領漢王諒府親信。

translations.literal: With his original rank he served as intimate of Prince of Han Liang's household.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a trusted officer in Prince of Han Yang Liang's household.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，諒舉兵作亂，仁基苦諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Liang raised troops in rebellion; Renji remonstrated bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Yang Liang rebelled. Renji remonstrated fiercely.

sentences.zh: 諒大怒，囚之於獄。

translations.literal: Liang was greatly enraged and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was furious and threw him in prison.

sentences.zh: 及諒敗，帝嘉之，超拜護軍。

translations.literal: When Liang was defeated, the Emperor praised him and promoted him to Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell, the emperor praised him and promoted him to Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 數歲，改授武賁郎將，從將軍李景討叛蠻向思多於黔安，以功進位銀青光祿大夫，賜奴婢百口，絹五百匹。

translations.literal: Several years later he was reassigned Brave Attendant General and followed General Li Jing to attack the rebel barbarian Xiang Siduo in Qian'an; for merit he was advanced to Silver-Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and granted a hundred household slaves and five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he became a Brave Attendant General and followed Li Jing against the rebel Xiang Siduo in Qian'an. For merit he rose to Silver-Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with a hundred slaves and five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 擊吐谷渾於張掖，破之，加授金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He attacked the Tuyuhun at Zhangye, defeated them, and was further appointed Gold-Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the Tuyuhun at Zhangye, defeated them, and was made Gold-Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 斬獲寇掠靺鞨，拜左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He beheaded and captured Mohe raiders and was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Mohe raiders and was made Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從征高麗，進位光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Goguryeo and was advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against Goguryeo and rose to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，李密據洛口，令仁基為河南道討捕大使，據武牢以拒密。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went to Jiangdu, Li Mi held Luokou and made Renji Grand Ambassador for Suppression and Capture on the Henan Circuit, holding Wulao to resist Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Jiangdu, Li Mi held Luokou and appointed Renji Grand Ambassador for Henan suppression, holding Wulao against Mi.

sentences.zh: 及滎陽通守張須陁為密所殺，仁基悉收其眾，每與密戰，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: When Xingyang Acting Prefect Zhang Xuotuo was killed by Mi, Renji gathered all his troops; each time he fought Mi he killed and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Xuotuo was killed, Renji absorbed his troops. In repeated clashes with Mi he killed and captured many.

sentences.zh: 時隋大亂，有功者不錄。

translations.literal: At the time the Sui was in great disorder and those with merit were not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui court was collapsing and meritorious service went unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 仁基見強寇在前，士卒勞敝，所得軍資，即用分賞。

translations.literal: Renji saw a strong bandit before him and his soldiers weary; whatever military goods he obtained he at once distributed as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Facing a powerful enemy with exhausted troops, Renji gave all captured supplies directly to his men.

sentences.zh: 監軍御史蕭懷靜每抑止之，眾咸怨怒。

translations.literal: Supervising Army Censor Xiao Huaijing always restrained this; the host all resented and raged.
translations.idiomatic: Army censor Xiao Huaijing kept blocking the payouts. The troops grew furious.

sentences.zh: 懷靜又陰持仁基長短，欲有所奏劾。

translations.literal: Huaijing also secretly kept track of Renji's faults and weaknesses, intending to memorialize and impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijing also gathered evidence against Renji for an impeachment memorial.

sentences.zh: 仁基懼，遂殺懷靜，以其眾歸密。

translations.literal: Renji was afraid; he therefore killed Huaijing and led his troops to submit to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing impeachment, Renji killed Huaijing and defected to Mi with his troops.

sentences.zh: 密以為河東郡公。

translations.literal: Mi made him Duke of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mi made him Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 其子行儼，驍勇善戰，密復以為絳郡公，甚相委昵。

translations.literal: His son Xingyan was fierce and brave in battle; Mi again made him Duke of Jiang Commandery and trusted him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingyan was a fierce warrior. Mi made him Duke of Jiang and favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 王世充以東都食盡，悉眾詣偃師，與密決戰。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong, because the Eastern Capital's grain was exhausted, led his entire host to Yanshi to fight a decisive battle with Mi.
translations.idiomatic: With the Eastern Capital starving, Wang Shichong marched his whole army to Yanshi for a decisive battle with Mi.

sentences.zh: 密問計於諸將，仁基對曰：「世充盡銳而至，洛下必虛，可分兵守其要路，令不得東。

translations.literal: Mi asked the generals for plans. Renji replied: "Shichong brings his entire sharp force; Luoyang below must be empty. Divide the army to hold the critical roads so he cannot go east.
translations.idiomatic: Mi asked his generals for counsel. Renji said: "Shichong brings everything he has. Luoyang must be empty. Hold the key roads so he cannot return east.

sentences.zh: 簡精兵三萬，傍河西出，以逼東都。

translations.literal: Choose thirty thousand picked troops, go out along the west bank of the river, and press the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Take thirty thousand elite troops west along the river and threaten the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 世充却還，我且按甲，世充重出，我又逼之。

translations.literal: When Shichong turns back, we hold our armor; when Shichong comes out again, we press him again.
translations.idiomatic: When he turns back we rest. When he marches out again we strike again.

sentences.zh: 如此則此有餘力，彼勞奔命，兵法所謂『彼出我歸，彼歸我出，數戰以疲之，多方以誤之』者也。」

translations.literal: Thus we have strength to spare while he wearies in forced marches—the art of war's "when he goes out we return, when he returns we go out, fight many times to wear him down, use many stratagems to confuse him."
translations.idiomatic: We keep our strength while he exhausts himself—the classic strategy: when he advances we withdraw, when he withdraws we advance, wear him down with repeated strikes and confuse him with many moves."

sentences.zh: 密曰：「公知其一，不知其二。

translations.literal: Mi said: "You know one but not two.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "You see one part, not the whole.

sentences.zh: 東都兵馬有三不可當：器械精，一也；

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital's troops and horses have three things that cannot be withstood: refined weapons—one;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital troops have three unbeatable advantages: first, fine weapons;

sentences.zh: 決計而來，二也；

translations.literal: they come with a fixed plan—two;
translations.idiomatic: second, they come determined to fight;

sentences.zh: 食盡求鬬，三也。

translations.literal: grain exhausted, they seek battle—three.
translations.idiomatic: third, they are starving and desperate.

sentences.zh: 我按甲蓄力，以觀其敝，彼求鬬不得，欲走無路，不過十日，世充之首可懸於麾下。」

translations.literal: We hold our armor and store strength to watch their exhaustion; they seek battle and cannot obtain it, wish to flee but have no road—in no more than ten days Shichong's head can be hung beneath our standard."
translations.idiomatic: We wait and let them wear themselves out. They cannot get the fight they want and cannot escape. In ten days Shichong's head will hang from our standard."

sentences.zh: 單雄信等諸將輕世充，皆請戰，仁基苦爭不得。

translations.literal: Shan Xiongxin and the other generals looked down on Shichong and all asked for battle; Renji argued bitterly but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin and the others despised Shichong and demanded battle. Renji argued in vain.

sentences.zh: 密難違諸將之言，戰遂大敗，仁基為世充所虜。

translations.literal: Mi found it hard to go against the generals' words; the battle ended in great defeat, and Renji was captured by Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Mi could not overrule them. The army was crushed and Renji was taken by Shichong.

sentences.zh: 世充以其父子並驍銳，深禮之，以兄女妻行儼。

translations.literal: Shichong because father and son were both fierce and sharp treated them with deep courtesy and gave his elder brother's daughter in marriage to Xingyan.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong honored them for their fighting prowess and married his niece to Xingyan.

sentences.zh: 及僭尊號，署仁基為禮部尚書，行儼為左輔大將軍。

translations.literal: When he usurped the imperial title he appointed Renji Minister of Rites and Xingyan Left Assistant Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong declared himself emperor he made Renji Minister of Rites and Xingyan Left Assistant Grand General.

sentences.zh: 行儼每有攻戰，所當皆披麾，號為「萬人敵」。

translations.literal: Whenever Xingyan attacked in battle, wherever he went he swept the banners; he was styled "Match for Ten Thousand."
translations.idiomatic: In battle Xingyan swept all before him and was called "Match for Ten Thousand Men."

sentences.zh: 世充憚其威名，頗加猜防。

translations.literal: Shichong feared his martial renown and added much suspicion and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong feared his fame and watched him closely.

sentences.zh: 仁基知其意，不自安，遂與世充所署尚書左丞宇文儒童、尚食直長陳謙、祕書丞崔德本等謀反，令陳謙於上食之際，持匕首以劫世充，行儼以兵應於階下。

translations.literal: Renji knew his intent and was ill at ease; he therefore with Shichong's appointed Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs Yuwen Rutong, Chief of Imperial Provisions Chen Qian, Secretariat Assistant Cui Deben, and others plotted rebellion, ordering Chen Qian at the time of serving food to seize a dagger and hold Shichong hostage while Xingyan responded with troops on the steps below.
translations.idiomatic: Renji sensed the danger and plotted with Yuwen Rutong, Chen Qian, Cui Deben, and others to stab Shichong at dinner while Xingyan rose on the steps with troops.

sentences.zh: 指麾事定，然後出越王侗以輔之。

translations.literal: Once the command was settled they would then bring out Prince of Yue Tong to assist in rule.
translations.idiomatic: Once the coup succeeded they would install Prince of Yue Yang Tong as ruler.

sentences.zh: 事臨發，將軍張童仁知其謀而告之，俱為世充所殺。

translations.literal: When the affair was about to break out, General Zhang Tongren learned of the plot and reported it; all were killed by Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the plot Zhang Tongren betrayed them. Shichong executed them all.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古先帝王之興也，非夫至德深仁格於天地，有豐功博利，弘濟艱難，不然，則其道無由矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When the ancient sage emperors and kings arose, was it not because supreme virtue and deep benevolence accorded with Heaven and Earth, because there were vast achievements and broad benefits that broadly relieved hardship—otherwise their Way had no source?
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Sage kings rise only when supreme virtue moves heaven and earth, or when vast merit relieves great hardship. Without that, there is no mandate.

sentences.zh: 自周邦不競，隋運將隆，武元、高祖並著大功於王室，平南國，摧東夏，總百揆，定三方，然後變謳歌，遷寶鼎。

translations.literal: From the time the Zhou house lost its contest and the Sui fortune was about to rise, Wu Yuan and Gaozu both achieved great merit in the royal house—pacifying the southern states, crushing the eastern Xia, overseeing all duties, settling the three regions—then they changed the songs of praise and moved the sacred tripod.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou declined and Sui rose, Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen both served the dynasty with great merit—pacifying the south, crushing the east, governing the realm, securing the three regions—then they took the throne.

sentences.zh: 于時匈奴驕倨，勾吳不朝，既爭長於黃池，亦飲馬於清渭。

translations.literal: At that time the Xiongnu were arrogant and Gou Wu did not attend court; they vied for precedence at Huangchi and also watered their horses at the clear Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu grew arrogant; Wu did not pay court. They contested supremacy at Huangchi and watered horses on the Wei.

sentences.zh: 高祖內綏外禦，曰不暇給，委心膂於俊傑，寄折衝於爪牙，文武爭馳，羣策畢舉。

translations.literal: Within, Gaozu soothed and without defended; he had no leisure even to eat, entrusting his heart and backbone to outstanding men, committing the breaking of enemy spears to his claws and fangs—civil and military strove forward, all stratagems were deployed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu defended within and without, scarcely pausing to eat. He trusted his best men with power and war. Civil and military officers strove together; every stratagem was tried.

sentences.zh: 服猾夏之虜，掃黃旗之寇，峻五岳以作鎮，環四海以為池，厚澤被於域中，餘威震於殊俗。

translations.literal: He subdued the crafty Xia captives, swept the yellow-banner bandits, made the Five Peaks his ramparts, took the four seas as his moat—thick favor spread within the realm, residual might shook distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: He subdued barbarians and rebels, made the Five Sacred Peaks his walls and the four seas his moat. His grace filled the realm; his might shook distant lands.

sentences.zh: 煬帝蒙故業，踐丕基，阻伊、洛而固崤、函，跨兩都而總萬國。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang inherited the old enterprise and trod the great foundation, blocking Yi and Luo while securing Xiao and Han, spanning the two capitals while overseeing ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang inherited a secure throne, held the passes of Yi and Luo and Xiao and Han, and ruled from two capitals over the realm.

sentences.zh: 矜曆數之在己，忽王業之艱難，不務以道恤人，將以申威海外。

translations.literal: He prized that the mandate of number was his, neglected the hardship of royal enterprise, did not strive to comfort the people by the Way, but meant to display might overseas.
translations.idiomatic: He thought the mandate was his alone, ignored the burden of rule, refused to govern with kindness, and sought glory abroad.

sentences.zh: 運拒諫之智，騁飾非之辯，恥轍迹之未遠，忘德義之不修。

translations.literal: He wielded the wisdom that rejects remonstrance, displayed the eloquence that ornaments wrong, was ashamed that his wheel tracks did not reach far enough, and forgot to cultivate virtue and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He rejected counsel, excused his faults, chased ever farther campaigns, and forgot virtue.

sentences.zh: 於是鑿通渠，開馳道，樹以柳杞，隱以金槌。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dug the canal, opened the imperial road, planted willows and jujubes, and concealed golden mallets.
translations.idiomatic: He dug the Grand Canal, built imperial highways, lined them with willows, and hid golden mallets in the banks.

sentences.zh: 西出玉門，東踰碣石，塹山堙谷，浮河達海。

translations.literal: West he went out through Jade Gate, east he crossed Jieshi, cutting through mountains and filling valleys, floating the river to reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He went west through Jade Gate and east beyond Jieshi, cutting mountains, filling valleys, and channeling rivers to the sea.

sentences.zh: 民力凋盡，徭戍無期，率土之心，鳥驚魚潰。

translations.literal: The people's strength was exhausted; corvée and garrison had no end; the heart of the realm—birds startled, fish scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The people were exhausted. Labor and garrison duty never ended. The realm panicked like startled birds and scattered fish.

sentences.zh: 方西規奄蔡，南討流求，親總八狄之師，屢踐三韓之域。

translations.literal: West he planned against Yan and Cai, south he campaigned against Liuqiu, personally leading the armies of the eight Di, repeatedly treading the lands of the three Han.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned west against Yan and Cai and south against Liuqiu, leading barbarian armies again and again into Korea.

sentences.zh: 自以威行萬物，顧指無違，又躬為長君，功高曩列，寵不假於外戚，權不逮於羣下，足以𨏼轢軒、唐，奄吞周、漢，子孫萬代，人莫能窺，振古以來，一君而已。
