translations.literal: He thought his might moved the ten thousand things and his glance brooked no denial; again he was the supreme ruler in person, his merit higher than past ranks, favor not lent to external kin, power not reaching to subordinates—enough to trample Xuanyuan and Tang, swallow Zhou and Han, ten thousand generations of descendants none could spy, from antiquity until now one ruler alone.
translations.idiomatic: He thought nothing could resist him. He outranked all past emperors, needed no in-laws, feared no minister—sure he surpassed the sage kings and would rule forever, unmatched in history.

sentences.zh: 遂乃外疎猛士，內忌忠良，恥有盜竊之聲，惡聞喪亂之事。

translations.literal: Thereupon outwardly he kept fierce warriors at a distance, inwardly he resented loyal and good men, was ashamed of reports of theft, and hated to hear of disorder and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He distrusted his best fighters, hated loyal ministers, punished news of theft, and refused to hear of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 出師命將，不料眾寡，兵少力屈者，以畏懦受顯誅，竭誠克勝者，以功高蒙隱戮。

translations.literal: When he sent out armies and ordered generals he did not gauge numbers; those with few troops whose strength failed were executed for cowardice, while those who exhausted loyalty and won were secretly punished for high merit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent generals out without regard to odds. Defeated commanders were executed for cowardice; victorious ones were punished for overshadowing him.

sentences.zh: 或斃鋒刃之下，或殞鴆毒之中，賞不可以有功求，刑不可以無罪免，畏首畏尾，進退維谷。

translations.literal: Some died beneath blades, some perished by poisoned wine—rewards could not be sought for merit, punishments could not be escaped for innocence; they feared head and feared tail, advance and retreat were both distress.
translations.idiomatic: Some died in battle, some by poison. Merit won no reward; innocence won no pardon. Officers feared to advance and feared to retreat.

sentences.zh: 彼山東之羣盜，多出厮役之中，無尺土之資，十家之產，豈有陳涉亡秦之志，張角亂漢之謀哉！

translations.literal: Those bandits east of the mountains mostly came from among corvée laborers, without a foot of land's assets or ten households' wealth—how could they have had Chen She's will to destroy Qin or Zhang Jue's plot to disorder Han!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels east of the mountains were mostly conscripts with no land and no wealth—what did they have of Chen She's ambition to topple Qin or Zhang Jue's plot to ruin Han!"

sentences.zh: 皆苦於上欲無厭，下不堪命，飢寒交切，救死雈蒲。

translations.literal: All suffered from the ruler's insatiable desires above and unbearable commands below; hunger and cold pressed together—they rushed to save their lives like duckweed.
translations.idiomatic: They suffered the emperor's endless demands above and unbearable orders below, hunger and cold together, and fled to save their lives.

sentences.zh: 莫識旌旗什伍之容，安知行師用兵之勢！

translations.literal: None knew the appearance of banners and ranks of five and ten; how could they know the momentum of marching armies and using troops!"
translations.idiomatic: They knew nothing of military drill or command. How could they understand formal warfare!"

sentences.zh: 但人自為戰，眾怒難犯，故攻無完城，野無橫陣，星離棊布，以千百數。

translations.literal: But each man fought for himself; the multitude's rage was hard to offend—therefore in attack no city was intact, in the wild no battle line held; scattered like stars, arrayed like chess pieces, they numbered in thousands and hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each fought for himself and collective rage was unstoppable. No walled city held; no field army stood. They spread like stars—thousands upon thousands.

sentences.zh: 豪傑因其機以動之，乘其勢而用之，雖有勇敢之士，明智之將，連踵覆沒，莫之能禦。

translations.literal: Heroes seized the moment to move them, rode the momentum to use them—though there were brave men and wise generals, they fell in succession and none could withstand.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes seized the moment and turned the tide. Brave commanders fell one after another and could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 煬帝魂褫氣懾，望絕兩京，謀竄身於江湖，襲永嘉之舊迹。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang's soul was stripped of courage and his breath cowed; hope of the two capitals was cut off; he planned to steal his body to rivers and lakes, following the old traces of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang lost heart and abandoned the two capitals, planning to flee south as the Jin court had fled at Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 既而禍生轂下，釁起舟中，思早告而莫追，唯請死而獲可。

translations.literal: Before long calamity arose beneath the carriage hub and strife rose in the boat; he wished to report early but could not overtake it—only to beg death and obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebellion struck at the capital and mutiny aboard his ship. He could not outrun disaster—he could only beg for death.

sentences.zh: 身棄南巢之野，首懸白旗之上，子孫勦絕，宗廟為墟。

translations.literal: His body was cast aside in the wilds south of the Nest; his head hung upon the white banner; descendants were exterminated; the ancestral temple became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: He died abandoned in the wilderness. His head hung from a white flag. His line was cut off and the ancestral temple lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 夫以開皇之初，比於大業之盛，度土地之廣狹，料戶口之眾寡，算甲兵之多少，校倉廩之虛實，九鼎之譬鴻毛，未喻輕重，培塿之方嵩岱，曾何等級！

translations.literal: To compare the beginning of Kaihuang with the splendor of Daye—measuring the breadth of land, estimating the multitude of households, counting armor and weapons, comparing granaries full or empty—the nine tripods against a goose feather cannot express light and heavy; a mound beside Mount Song—what rank could they share!
translations.idiomatic: Compare Kaihuang at its height with Daye at its peak—land, population, arms, granaries. The nine tripods beside a goose feather, a molehill beside Mount Song: the gap is beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 論地險則遼隧未擬於長江，語人謀則勾麗不侔於陳國。

translations.literal: Speaking of terrain's danger, Liaosui could not be compared to the Yangzi; speaking of human planning, Goguryeo could not match Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In terrain, Liaodong was no match for the Yangzi campaign; in strategy, Goguryeo was no match for Chen.

sentences.zh: 高祖掃江南以清六合，煬帝事遼東而喪天下。

translations.literal: Gaozu swept the south of the river to clear the six harmonies; Emperor Yang campaigned in Liaodong and lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu pacified the south and united the realm. Emperor Yang campaigned in Liaodong and lost it.

sentences.zh: 其故何哉？

translations.literal: What is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 所為之迹同，所用之心異也。

translations.literal: The traces of their actions were the same; the hearts they employed were different.
translations.idiomatic: Their actions looked alike; their intentions did not.

sentences.zh: 高祖北却強胡，南并百越，十有餘載，戎車屢動，民亦勞止，不為無事。

translations.literal: Gaozu northward repelled strong Hu, southward merged the hundred Yue—more than ten years, war chariots moved repeatedly, the people also labored and stopped; it was not that there were no affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu fought the northern barbarians and absorbed the south for more than ten years. The people labored; wars were frequent. He was not idle.

sentences.zh: 然其動也，思以安之，其勞也，思以逸之。

translations.literal: Yet when he moved, he thought to settle the people in peace; when he labored them, he thought to give them rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he campaigned he meant to bring peace; when he burdened them he meant to give rest afterward.

sentences.zh: 是以民致時雍，師無怨讟，誠在於愛利，故其興也勃焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the people attained timely harmony; the army had no complaints—the sincerity lay in love and benefit, therefore his rise was swift.
translations.idiomatic: The people prospered and the army did not mutter. He ruled through care and reward, and his rise was swift.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣承平之基，守已安之業，肆其淫放，虐用其民，視億兆如草芥，顧羣臣如寇讎，勞近以事遠，求名而喪實。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang succeeded a peaceful foundation and guarded an already settled enterprise, indulged his debauchery, cruelly used the people, regarded the hundred millions as grass and stalks, looked on his ministers as bandit-enemies, labored what was near to serve what was far, sought name and lost substance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang inherited peace, then squandered it in debauchery, treated the people like grass and his ministers like enemies, exhausted the near to serve the far, and sought glory without substance.

sentences.zh: 兵纏魏闕，阽危弗圖，圍解雁門，慢遊不息。

translations.literal: Armies entangled at the Wei gate; peril on the brink he did not plan; the siege at Wild Goose Gate was lifted, yet he roamed slowly without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion reached the capital yet he would not act. After the siege at Wild Goose Gate he still wandered without urgency.

sentences.zh: 天奪之魄，人益其災，羣盜並興，百殃俱起，自絕民神之望，故其亡也忽焉。

translations.literal: Heaven took his soul; men increased his calamity; bandits rose together, a hundred disasters all arose—he cut off the hope of people and spirits, therefore his perishing was sudden.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven withdrew its favor; men piled disaster on disaster. Rebels rose on every side. He lost the people and gods, and his fall was sudden.

sentences.zh: 訊之古老，考其行事，此高祖之所由興，而煬帝之所以滅者也。

translations.literal: Inquire of the ancients, examine their conduct—this is what Gaozu rose by, and what Emperor Yang perished by.
translations.idiomatic: Ask the ancients and weigh their deeds: this is how Gaozu rose and how Emperor Yang fell.

sentences.zh: 可不謂然乎！

translations.literal: Can it not be called so!
translations.idiomatic: Is it not so!

sentences.zh: 其隋之得失存亡，大較與秦相類。

translations.literal: The Sui's gain and loss, survival and perishing, in the main resemble Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's rise and fall largely mirror Qin's.

sentences.zh: 始皇并吞六國，高祖統一九州，二世虐用威刑，煬帝肆行猜毒，皆禍起於羣盜，而身殞於匹夫。

translations.literal: The First Emperor swallowed and merged the six states; Gaozu unified the nine regions. The Second Emperor cruelly used punitive power; Emperor Yang wantonly practiced suspicious poison—both calamities arose from bandit hosts and both bodies perished at the hands of common men.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor united six states; Gaozu united the realm. The Second Emperor ruled by terror; Emperor Yang ruled by suspicion. Both were brought down by rebels and died at common hands.

sentences.zh: 原始要終，若合符契矣。

translations.literal: Tracing origin and seeking end, it is as if tally and seal matched.
translations.idiomatic: From beginning to end the parallel is exact.

sentences.zh: 玄感宰相之子，荷國重恩，君之失德，當竭股肱。

translations.literal: Xuangan was a prime minister's son who bore the state's heavy favor; when the ruler lost virtue he should have exhausted his limbs and trunk.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan was a minister's son favored by the state. When the emperor lost his way he should have given his life in service.

sentences.zh: 未議致身，先圖問鼎，遂假伊、霍之事，將肆莽、卓之心。

translations.literal: Before discussing giving his person, he first plotted to inquire of the tripod; he therefore borrowed the affairs of Yi and Huo, about to unleash the heart of Wang Mang and Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of serving faithfully he plotted usurpation, cloaking himself in Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou while acting like Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 人神同疾，敗不旋踵，兄弟就葅醢之誅，先人受焚如之酷，不亦甚乎！

translations.literal: Men and spirits alike hated him; defeat did not turn on its heel; brothers met minced-pickle execution; forebears received burning-like cruelty—is it not extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Men and gods alike reviled him. He fell in an instant. His brothers were butchered and his clan burned—is that not extreme enough!

sentences.zh: 李密遭會風雲，奮其鱗翼，思封函谷，將割鴻溝。

translations.literal: Li Mi encountered the meeting of wind and clouds, roused his scales and wings, thought to seal Hangu Pass and carve the Hong Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi rode the storm of the age, spread his wings, aimed to hold Hangu Pass and divide the empire like the warlords of old.

sentences.zh: 朞月之間，眾數十萬，破化及，摧世充，聲動四方，威行萬里。

translations.literal: Within a month's time his host numbered hundreds of thousands; he broke Huaji and crushed Shichong; his fame moved the four quarters, his might traveled ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he commanded hundreds of thousands, defeated Huaji, crushed Shichong, and shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 雖運乖天眷，事屈興王，而義協人謀，雄名克振，壯矣！

translations.literal: Though fortune opposed heaven's favor and affairs bent the rise of kings, yet righteousness accorded with men's plans and heroic name could be raised—how grand!
translations.idiomatic: Though heaven denied him the throne, his cause won men's hearts and his fame endures—magnificent!

sentences.zh: 然志性輕狡，終致顛覆，其度長挈大，抑陳、項之季孟歟？

translations.literal: Yet his will and nature were light and cunning; in the end he met overturn—is his measuring length and grasping weight perhaps the elder and younger of Chen and Xiang?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was rash and cunning and fell in the end. Compared with Chen Sheng and Xiang Yu, where does he rank?
